{{Editorial_Status|status=approved|reviewer=APF Editorial & Peer Review Council|date=2026-09-08}} {{APF_Competency_Badge|competency=Futuring}} {{Infobox Foresight Method | name = Causal Layered Analysis (CLA) | originator = Sohail Inayatullah (1998) | year_introduced = Tamkang University / Metafuture | apf_competency = Futuring | paradigm = Exploratory, Plausible & Critical Foresight | horizon_focus = Horizon 2 / Horizon 3 | time_horizon = 5–25 Years | format = Expert Facilitated Workshop / Analytical Modeling | complexity = Intermediate to Advanced | outputs = Prioritized driver maps, scenario matrices, robust strategic pathways | related_methods = [[The Futures Cone]], [[Causal Layered Analysis (CLA)|CLA]], [[The Three Horizons Framework (Bill Sharpe)|Three Horizons]] }} == Executive Summary & Definition == '''Causal Layered Analysis (CLA)''' is an authoritative subject within '''Core Foresight Methodologies & Frameworks''' and forms a vital component of the global canon stewarded by the '''Association of Professional Futurists (APF)'''. Classified under the [[Category:APF Competency - Futuring|APF Core Competency: Futuring]], this entry provides strategic practitioners, institutional leaders, and policy analysts with an actionable, theoretically grounded understanding of its mechanisms and real-world utility. A poststructural foresight methodology deconstructing issues across four vertical depths: Litany, Systemic Causes, Worldview/Discourse, and Myth/Metaphor. == Origins & Theoretical Lineage == Developed by Pakistani-Australian futurist Sohail Inayatullah in his seminal 1998 paper 'Causal Layered Analysis: Poststructuralism as Method' in Futures. Drawing from poststructuralist philosophy (Michel Foucault, P.R. Sarkar, and feminist critique), CLA overcomes the shallow empiricism of traditional forecasting by demonstrating that lasting systemic transformation requires excavating and transforming deep cultural myths and unconscious metaphors. == Step-by-Step Facilitation & Execution Architecture == Executing '''Causal Layered Analysis (CLA)''' requires a disciplined, multistage facilitation process to ensure analytical rigor and deep stakeholder engagement: # '''Step 1''': Level 1 - The Litany: Surface-level data, alarming headlines, and official statistics that evoke immediate emotional reactions without systemic context. # '''Step 2''': Level 2 - Social / Systemic Causes: The institutional, economic, political, and historical structures that generate the litany (e.g., market incentives, laws). # '''Step 3''': Level 3 - Worldview / Discourse: The philosophical paradigms, epistemic frameworks, cultural values, and ideological assumptions that legitimize the system. # '''Step 4''': Level 4 - Myth / Metaphor: The visceral, subconscious, archetypal narratives and emotional imagery that sustain the worldview. # '''Step 5''': Vertical Transformation: Facilitators guide participants down from Litany to Myth, transform the core metaphor into an empowering alternative, and rebuild back up. == Strategic, Policy & Organizational Applications == In applied organizational strategy, corporate innovation, and anticipatory governance, '''Causal Layered Analysis (CLA)''' is routinely utilized to: * Institutional Strategy: Uncovering why organizational transformation initiatives repeatedly fail due to unaddressed cultural myths. * Policy Deconstruction: Exposing the hidden ideological assumptions behind governmental defense, health, and education policies. * Cross-Cultural Conflict Resolution: Mediating entrenched social disputes by examining divergent cultural mythologies. * Speculative Worldbuilding: Crafting deeply authentic future worlds with aligned myths, discourses, institutions, and litanies. == Methodological Critique, Cognitive Biases & Failure Modes == While potent, the effective deployment of '''Causal Layered Analysis (CLA)''' requires vigilance regarding several critical failure modes and cognitive traps: * Metaphor Trivialization: Teams frequently treat Level 4 as mere creative branding rather than deep psycho-social excavation. * Facilitation Rigor: Requires advanced facilitators comfortable with navigating emotional, ideological, and cultural vulnerability. * Upward Rebuilding Neglect: Spending all workshop time deconstructing downward while neglecting to rebuild the new systemic level. == Alignment with the APF Foresight Competencies == Under the '''Association of Professional Futurists (APF) Competency Framework''', '''Causal Layered Analysis (CLA)''' directly reinforces: * '''Primary Competency (Futuring)''': Cultivates advanced professional rigor in executing futuring-related foresight workflows. * '''Complementary Competencies''': Synthesizes insights across [[Category:APF Competency - Framing|Framing]], [[Category:APF Competency - Scanning|Scanning]], [[Category:APF Competency - Futuring|Futuring]], [[Category:APF Competency - Designing|Designing]], [[Category:APF Competency - Adapting|Adapting]], and [[Category:APF Competency - Leading|Leading]]. == References & Recommended Reading ==
    {{Foresight_Citation|author=Inayatullah, S.|year=1998|title=Causal layered analysis: Poststructuralism as method|journal=Futures|volume=30|issue=8|pages=815-829|doi=10.1016/S0016-3287(98)00086-X}} {{Foresight_Citation|author=Inayatullah, S.|year=2004|title=The Causal Layered Analysis Reader: Theory and Case Studies|publisher=Tamkang University Press}}

{{Editorial_Status|status=approved|reviewer=APF Editorial & Peer Review Council|date=2026-09-08}} {{APF_Competency_Badge|competency=Futuring}} {{Infobox Foresight Method | name = The Delphi Method | originator = Norman Dalkey & Olaf Helmer (1950s/1963), Theodore Gordon | year_introduced = RAND Corporation / Project Delphi | apf_competency = Futuring | paradigm = Exploratory, Plausible & Critical Foresight | horizon_focus = Horizon 2 / Horizon 3 | time_horizon = 5–25 Years | format = Expert Facilitated Workshop / Analytical Modeling | complexity = Intermediate to Advanced | outputs = Prioritized driver maps, scenario matrices, robust strategic pathways | related_methods = [[The Futures Cone]], [[Causal Layered Analysis (CLA)|CLA]], [[The Three Horizons Framework (Bill Sharpe)|Three Horizons]] }} == Executive Summary & Definition == '''The Delphi Method''' is an authoritative subject within '''Core Foresight Methodologies & Frameworks''' and forms a vital component of the global canon stewarded by the '''Association of Professional Futurists (APF)'''. Classified under the [[Category:APF Competency - Futuring|APF Core Competency: Futuring]], this entry provides strategic practitioners, institutional leaders, and policy analysts with an actionable, theoretically grounded understanding of its mechanisms and real-world utility. A structured communication technique for eliciting and synthesizing expert consensus on complex, uncertain developments through iterative anonymous questionnaires. == Origins & Theoretical Lineage == Originating in the early 1950s at the RAND Corporation under Project Delphi, sponsored by the US Air Force to forecast the impact of nuclear weapons and military technology. Pioneered by mathematicians Norman Dalkey and Olaf Helmer, and declassified in 1963, Delphi rapidly became one of the most widely cited quantitative/semi-quantitative tools in futures research and technology assessment. == Step-by-Step Facilitation & Execution Architecture == Executing '''The Delphi Method''' requires a disciplined, multistage facilitation process to ensure analytical rigor and deep stakeholder engagement: # '''Step 1''': Round 1 - Open Exploration: A panel of geographically distributed experts receives open-ended questions soliciting forecasts, technological milestones, and timeframes. # '''Step 2''': Anonymity: Panelists do not interact directly or know each other's specific answers, eliminating peer pressure, bandwagon effects, and dominant personality bias. # '''Step 3''': Round 2 & 3 - Controlled Statistical Feedback: Anonymized responses and statistical distributions (medians, interquartile ranges) are presented back to the panel. Outliers must justify their positions. # '''Step 4''': Convergence & Synthesis: Panelists re-evaluate estimates in light of collective arguments. The process terminates when stable consensus or polarized clusters emerge. == Strategic, Policy & Organizational Applications == In applied organizational strategy, corporate innovation, and anticipatory governance, '''The Delphi Method''' is routinely utilized to: * Technology Roadmapping: Establishing consensus timelines for commercialization of quantum computing, fusion, and synthetic biology. * Clinical & Public Health Consensus: Determining future disease burden and pandemic preparedness guidelines. * National Science Policy: Prioritizing long-term public R&D funding allocations across competitive engineering domains. * Wild Card Assessment: Estimating probabilities and impact severities for low-frequency, high-consequence global threats. == Methodological Critique, Cognitive Biases & Failure Modes == While potent, the effective deployment of '''The Delphi Method''' requires vigilance regarding several critical failure modes and cognitive traps: * Panelist Attrition: Multi-round surveys running over months frequently suffer high dropout rates among elite domain experts. * Consensus Pressure: The statistical feedback mechanism can artificially suppress genuinely prophetic minority outlier perspectives. * Selection Bias: The composition of the expert panel heavily predetermines the outcome, reinforcing conventional orthodoxies. == Alignment with the APF Foresight Competencies == Under the '''Association of Professional Futurists (APF) Competency Framework''', '''The Delphi Method''' directly reinforces: * '''Primary Competency (Futuring)''': Cultivates advanced professional rigor in executing futuring-related foresight workflows. * '''Complementary Competencies''': Synthesizes insights across [[Category:APF Competency - Framing|Framing]], [[Category:APF Competency - Scanning|Scanning]], [[Category:APF Competency - Futuring|Futuring]], [[Category:APF Competency - Designing|Designing]], [[Category:APF Competency - Adapting|Adapting]], and [[Category:APF Competency - Leading|Leading]]. == References & Recommended Reading ==
    {{Foresight_Citation|author=Dalkey, N. & Helmer, O.|year=1963|title=An experimental application of the DELPHI method to the use of experts|journal=Management Science|volume=9|issue=3|pages=458-467|doi=10.1287/mnsc.9.3.458}} {{Foresight_Citation|author=Linstone, H. A. & Turoff, M.|year=1975|title=The Delphi Method: Techniques and Applications|publisher=Addison-Wesley}}
[[Category:APF Foresight Wiki]] [[Category:Core Foresight Methodologies & Frameworks]] [[Category:APF Competency - Futuring]] [[Category:APF Article Status - Approved]]

{{Editorial_Status|status=approved|reviewer=APF Editorial & Peer Review Council|date=2026-09-08}} {{APF_Competency_Badge|competency=Futuring}} {{Infobox Foresight Method | name = The Three Horizons Framework (Bill Sharpe) | originator = Bill Sharpe (2013), Andrew Curry & Anthony Hodgson (2008) | year_introduced = International Futures Forum (IFF) | apf_competency = Futuring | paradigm = Exploratory, Plausible & Critical Foresight | horizon_focus = Horizon 2 / Horizon 3 | time_horizon = 5–25 Years | format = Expert Facilitated Workshop / Analytical Modeling | complexity = Intermediate to Advanced | outputs = Prioritized driver maps, scenario matrices, robust strategic pathways | related_methods = [[The Futures Cone]], [[Causal Layered Analysis (CLA)|CLA]], [[The Three Horizons Framework (Bill Sharpe)|Three Horizons]] }} == Executive Summary & Definition == '''The Three Horizons Framework (Bill Sharpe)''' is an authoritative subject within '''Core Foresight Methodologies & Frameworks''' and forms a vital component of the global canon stewarded by the '''Association of Professional Futurists (APF)'''. Classified under the [[Category:APF Competency - Futuring|APF Core Competency: Futuring]], this entry provides strategic practitioners, institutional leaders, and policy analysts with an actionable, theoretically grounded understanding of its mechanisms and real-world utility. A dynamic facilitation and strategic dialogue model mapping how dominant operating systems decline and emergent systems arise across three temporal horizons. == Origins & Theoretical Lineage == Originally articulated in a business strategy context by Baghai, Coley, and White (McKinsey), the model was radically re-conceived as a futures transformation methodology by Anthony Hodgson, Andrew Curry, and philosopher Bill Sharpe at the International Futures Forum (IFF). In his 2013 book Three Horizons: The Patterning of Hope, Sharpe established it as a shared language connecting managerial pragmatism, entrepreneurial innovation, and visionary transformation. == Step-by-Step Facilitation & Execution Architecture == Executing '''The Three Horizons Framework (Bill Sharpe)''' requires a disciplined, multistage facilitation process to ensure analytical rigor and deep stakeholder engagement: # '''Step 1''': Horizon 1 (H1) - The Current Prevailing System: The established way of doing things that provides current stability but is losing fitness as conditions change. # '''Step 2''': Horizon 3 (H3) - The Emergent Transformative Future: The visionary seeds of a fundamentally new system already visible on the fringe today. # '''Step 3''': Horizon 2 (H2) - The Turbulent Transition Zone: The contested space of intermediate innovations, dilemmas, and market disruption. # '''Step 4''': H2+ vs. H2- Diagnostic: Crucial distinction—H2- innovations are captured by H1 to prolong the incumbent system, whereas H2+ innovations act as stepping stones enabling H3 transformation. # '''Step 5''': Collaborative Dialogue: Moving participants from defensive turf wars to recognizing that all three horizons must collaborate in the present. == Strategic, Policy & Organizational Applications == In applied organizational strategy, corporate innovation, and anticipatory governance, '''The Three Horizons Framework (Bill Sharpe)''' is routinely utilized to: * Organizational Transformation: Aligning legacy operations teams (H1), internal innovation labs (H2), and long-term strategy units (H3). * Health System Redesign: Transitioning from acute hospital-centric care (H1) through digital telehealth (H2) to preventative community wellness (H3). * Energy Grid Modernization: Moving from centralized fossil-fuel baseload (H1) through bridge gas/hybrid grids (H2) to distributed renewables (H3). * Public Sector Policy Reform: Designing legislative pathways that foster H2+ stepping-stone innovations while phasing out H1 subsidies. == Methodological Critique, Cognitive Biases & Failure Modes == While potent, the effective deployment of '''The Three Horizons Framework (Bill Sharpe)''' requires vigilance regarding several critical failure modes and cognitive traps: * Linear Horizon Compression: Treating H1, H2, and H3 as rigid sequential decades rather than concurrent mindsets existing in the present. * H2 Capture Vulnerability: Inability of workshop teams to distinguish between H2- sustaining innovations and true H2+ transformative innovations. * Visionary Alienation: H3 visions formulated without practical H2 stepping stones are dismissed by executive leadership as impractical fantasy. == Alignment with the APF Foresight Competencies == Under the '''Association of Professional Futurists (APF) Competency Framework''', '''The Three Horizons Framework (Bill Sharpe)''' directly reinforces: * '''Primary Competency (Futuring)''': Cultivates advanced professional rigor in executing futuring-related foresight workflows. * '''Complementary Competencies''': Synthesizes insights across [[Category:APF Competency - Framing|Framing]], [[Category:APF Competency - Scanning|Scanning]], [[Category:APF Competency - Futuring|Futuring]], [[Category:APF Competency - Designing|Designing]], [[Category:APF Competency - Adapting|Adapting]], and [[Category:APF Competency - Leading|Leading]]. == References & Recommended Reading ==
    {{Foresight_Citation|author=Sharpe, B.|year=2013|title=Three Horizons: The Patterning of Hope|publisher=Triarchy Press}} {{Foresight_Citation|author=Curry, A. & Hodgson, A.|year=2008|title=Seeing in multiple horizons: Connecting futures to strategy|journal=Journal of Futures Studies|volume=13|issue=1|pages=1-20}}

Robinson (1982, 1990) | year_introduced = University of British Columbia | apf_competency = Futuring | paradigm = Exploratory, Plausible & Critical Foresight | horizon_focus = Horizon 2 / Horizon 3 | time_horizon = 5–25 Years | format = Expert Facilitated Workshop / Analytical Modeling | complexity = Intermediate to Advanced | outputs = Prioritized driver maps, scenario matrices, robust strategic pathways | related_methods = [[The Futures Cone]], [[Causal Layered Analysis (CLA)|CLA]], [[The Three Horizons Framework (Bill Sharpe)|Three Horizons]] }} == Executive Summary & Definition == '''Backcasting (John B. Robinson)''' is an authoritative subject within '''Core Foresight Methodologies & Frameworks''' and forms a vital component of the global canon stewarded by the '''Association of Professional Futurists (APF)'''. Classified under the [[Category:APF Competency - Futuring|APF Core Competency: Futuring]], this entry provides strategic practitioners, institutional leaders, and policy analysts with an actionable, theoretically grounded understanding of its mechanisms and real-world utility. A normative planning methodology that defines a desirable, sustainable future goal and works backwards to identify the required strategic milestones. == Origins & Theoretical Lineage == Developed by Canadian energy analyst John B. Robinson in the early 1980s as a counterpoint to conventional energy forecasting, which consistently extrapolated rising fossil fuel consumption. Robinson showed that forecasting was fundamentally biased toward reproducing the status quo. Backcasting shifts the paradigm: rather than asking 'Where will trends take us?', it asks 'What future do we want, and how can we build a feasible path to achieve it?' == Step-by-Step Facilitation & Execution Architecture == Executing '''Backcasting (John B. Robinson)''' requires a disciplined, multistage facilitation process to ensure analytical rigor and deep stakeholder engagement: # '''Step 1''': Stage 1 - Normative Visioning: Articulating a rigorous, internally consistent, and desirable future end-state (e.g., net-zero circular city in 2050). # '''Step 2''': Stage 2 - Feasibility & Sustainability Criteria: Establishing strict physical, ecological, social, and economic boundary conditions that the vision must respect. # '''Step 3''': Stage 3 - Reverse Milestone Mapping: Tracing backwards from 2050 to 2040, 2035, 2030, and 2025, identifying critical institutional decisions and inflection points. # '''Step 4''': Stage 4 - Gap & Obstacle Analysis: Identifying current policy lock-ins, institutional veto players, and market barriers that obstruct the backcasted pathway. # '''Step 5''': Stage 5 - Near-Term Action Agenda: Deriving immediate strategic actions, pilot projects, and regulatory changes required in the next 12-36 months. == Strategic, Policy & Organizational Applications == In applied organizational strategy, corporate innovation, and anticipatory governance, '''Backcasting (John B. Robinson)''' is routinely utilized to: * Net-Zero Decarbonization Pathways: Formulating municipal and national climate neutrality roadmaps for 2050. * Circular Economy Infrastructure: Backcasting resource recovery milestones from zero-waste industrial mandates. * Urban Transportation Planning: Designing transit-oriented cities by working backwards from automobile-free urban centers. * Corporate Long-Range Strategy: Reverse-engineering capital investments required to achieve bold 20-year moonshot goals. == Methodological Critique, Cognitive Biases & Failure Modes == While potent, the effective deployment of '''Backcasting (John B. Robinson)''' requires vigilance regarding several critical failure modes and cognitive traps: * Wishful Thinking Fallacy: Drafting utopian end-state visions that violate thermodynamic, material, or economic physical laws. * Technological Determinism: Assuming breakthrough bridge technologies will automatically materialize exactly on the required schedule. * Political Resistance: Near-term incumbent lobbies blocking the necessary near-term policy interventions required to open the path. == Alignment with the APF Foresight Competencies == Under the '''Association of Professional Futurists (APF) Competency Framework''', '''Backcasting (John B. Robinson)''' directly reinforces: * '''Primary Competency (Futuring)''': Cultivates advanced professional rigor in executing futuring-related foresight workflows. * '''Complementary Competencies''': Synthesizes insights across [[Category:APF Competency - Framing|Framing]], [[Category:APF Competency - Scanning|Scanning]], [[Category:APF Competency - Futuring|Futuring]], [[Category:APF Competency - Designing|Designing]], [[Category:APF Competency - Adapting|Adapting]], and [[Category:APF Competency - Leading|Leading]]. == References & Recommended Reading ==
    {{Foresight_Citation|author=Robinson, J. B.|year=1982|title=Energy backcasting: A proposed method of policy analysis|journal=Energy Policy|volume=10|issue=4|pages=337-344|doi=10.1016/0301-4215(82)90048-9}} {{Foresight_Citation|author=Robinson, J. B.|year=1990|title=Futures under glass: A recipe for people who hate to predict|journal=Futures|volume=22|issue=8|pages=820-842|doi=10.1016/0016-3287(90)90018-D}}

{{Editorial_Status|status=approved|reviewer=APF Editorial & Peer Review Council|date=2026-09-08}} {{APF_Competency_Badge|competency=Futuring}} {{Infobox Foresight Method | name = The Futures Wheel (Jerome Glenn) | originator = Jerome C. Glenn (1971) | year_introduced = The Millennium Project | apf_competency = Futuring | paradigm = Exploratory, Plausible & Critical Foresight | horizon_focus = Horizon 2 / Horizon 3 | time_horizon = 5–25 Years | format = Expert Facilitated Workshop / Analytical Modeling | complexity = Intermediate to Advanced | outputs = Prioritized driver maps, scenario matrices, robust strategic pathways | related_methods = [[The Futures Cone]], [[Causal Layered Analysis (CLA)|CLA]], [[The Three Horizons Framework (Bill Sharpe)|Three Horizons]] }} == Executive Summary & Definition == '''The Futures Wheel (Jerome Glenn)''' is an authoritative subject within '''Core Foresight Methodologies & Frameworks''' and forms a vital component of the global canon stewarded by the '''Association of Professional Futurists (APF)'''. Classified under the [[Category:APF Competency - Futuring|APF Core Competency: Futuring]], this entry provides strategic practitioners, institutional leaders, and policy analysts with an actionable, theoretically grounded understanding of its mechanisms and real-world utility. A graphical brainstorming and impact-mapping technique used to identify the primary, secondary, and tertiary consequences of a specific future event or decision. == Origins & Theoretical Lineage == Invented in 1971 by Jerome C. Glenn while working on futures education curricula at the Antioch Graduate School of Education. As a founding leader of The Millennium Project and co-author of Futures Research Methodology, Glenn standardized the technique into one of the most widely utilized facilitation methods globally for exploring second- and third-order ripple effects. == Step-by-Step Facilitation & Execution Architecture == Executing '''The Futures Wheel (Jerome Glenn)''' requires a disciplined, multistage facilitation process to ensure analytical rigor and deep stakeholder engagement: # '''Step 1''': Center Hub: A single future event, policy change, or disruptive innovation is written in the central circle (e.g., 'Commercialization of Room-Temperature Superconductors'). # '''Step 2''': First Ring (Primary Impacts): 4 to 8 immediate, direct consequences radiating out from the center via single lines. # '''Step 3''': Second Ring (Secondary Impacts): Consequences resulting directly from the first-order impacts, drawn via double lines. # '''Step 4''': Third Ring (Tertiary Impacts): Systemic ripple effects resulting from secondary impacts, drawn via triple lines; this is where counter-intuitive insights emerge. # '''Step 5''': Cross-Impact & Feedback Analysis: Facilitators highlight arrows connecting disparate branches where secondary or tertiary impacts reinforce or counteract one another. == Strategic, Policy & Organizational Applications == In applied organizational strategy, corporate innovation, and anticipatory governance, '''The Futures Wheel (Jerome Glenn)''' is routinely utilized to: * Policy Impact Assessment: Uncovering unintended negative side-effects of proposed legislative acts before implementation. * Corporate Risk Management: Mapping how an emerging competitor's product will trigger secondary supply chain and pricing disruptions. * Crisis Simulation: Projecting the multi-order cascades of a severe cyber-attack or grid blackout. * Executive Foresight Training: Rapidly training non-futurists to appreciate non-linear systems thinking and delayed feedback loops. == Methodological Critique, Cognitive Biases & Failure Modes == While potent, the effective deployment of '''The Futures Wheel (Jerome Glenn)''' requires vigilance regarding several critical failure modes and cognitive traps: * Linear Branching Proliferation: Wheels can become visually chaotic and unreadable without disciplined facilitation and clustering. * Brainstorming Superficially: Participants often generate superficial first-ring impacts while failing to push deeply into non-obvious tertiary cascades. * Ignoring Negative Feedback: Tending to map purely runaway exponential effects while overlooking balancing feedback loops that dampen disruption. == Alignment with the APF Foresight Competencies == Under the '''Association of Professional Futurists (APF) Competency Framework''', '''The Futures Wheel (Jerome Glenn)''' directly reinforces: * '''Primary Competency (Futuring)''': Cultivates advanced professional rigor in executing futuring-related foresight workflows. * '''Complementary Competencies''': Synthesizes insights across [[Category:APF Competency - Framing|Framing]], [[Category:APF Competency - Scanning|Scanning]], [[Category:APF Competency - Futuring|Futuring]], [[Category:APF Competency - Designing|Designing]], [[Category:APF Competency - Adapting|Adapting]], and [[Category:APF Competency - Leading|Leading]]. == References & Recommended Reading ==
    {{Foresight_Citation|author=Glenn, J. C.|year=1972|title=Futurizing Teaching vs Futures Course|journal=Social Science Record|volume=9|issue=3|pages=26-29}} {{Foresight_Citation|author=Glenn, J. C.|year=2009|title=The Futures Wheel|publisher=Futures Research Methodology Version 3.0}}

{{Editorial_Status|status=approved|reviewer=APF Editorial & Peer Review Council|date=2026-09-08}} {{APF_Competency_Badge|competency=Futuring}} {{Infobox Foresight Method | name = Real-Time Delphi (RTD) | originator = Theodore Gordon, Jerome Glenn | year_introduced = The Millennium Project | apf_competency = Futuring | paradigm = Exploratory, Plausible & Critical Foresight | horizon_focus = Horizon 2 / Horizon 3 | time_horizon = 5–25 Years | format = Expert Facilitated Workshop / Analytical Modeling | complexity = Intermediate to Advanced | outputs = Prioritized driver maps, scenario matrices, robust strategic pathways | related_methods = [[The Futures Cone]], [[Causal Layered Analysis (CLA)|CLA]], [[The Three Horizons Framework (Bill Sharpe)|Three Horizons]] }} == Executive Summary & Definition == '''Real-Time Delphi (RTD)''' is an authoritative subject within '''Core Foresight Methodologies & Frameworks''' and forms a vital component of the global canon stewarded by the '''Association of Professional Futurists (APF)'''. Classified under the [[Category:APF Competency - Futuring|APF Core Competency: Futuring]], this entry provides strategic practitioners, institutional leaders, and policy analysts with an actionable, theoretically grounded understanding of its mechanisms and real-world utility. 'Real-Time Delphi (RTD)' is a rigorously standardized methodology within professional strategic foresight. == Origins & Theoretical Lineage == Pioneered by Theodore Gordon, Jerome Glenn within The Millennium Project, this framework provides structured heuristics for interrogating uncertainty, navigating alternative futures, and translating anticipatory intelligence into decision-making. == Step-by-Step Facilitation & Execution Architecture == Executing '''Real-Time Delphi (RTD)''' requires a disciplined, multistage facilitation process to ensure analytical rigor and deep stakeholder engagement: # '''Step 1''': Stage 1 - Focal Framing & Scoping: Clarifying the core strategic challenge, decision horizon, and participant composition under Theodore Gordon, Jerome Glenn's guidelines. # '''Step 2''': Stage 2 - Environmental Scanning & Evidence Harvesting: Gathering cross-cutting systemic signals and qualitative drivers. # '''Step 3''': Stage 3 - Structural Mapping & Analysis: Deploying analytical matrices to challenge linear assumptions and map feedback loops. # '''Step 4''': Stage 4 - Scenario Generation / Synthesis: Constructing robust narrative or computational models of alternative possibilities. # '''Step 5''': Stage 5 - Strategy Stress-Testing & Action: Wind-tunneling current plans against generated futures to derive adaptive contingencies. == Strategic, Policy & Organizational Applications == In applied organizational strategy, corporate innovation, and anticipatory governance, '''Real-Time Delphi (RTD)''' is routinely utilized to: * Corporate Strategy & Innovation: Stress-testing multi-year investments against alternative operating environments. * Anticipatory Governance & Public Policy: Formulating agile, adaptive legislation capable of responding to emergent shocks. * Risk Management & Resilience: Identifying high-consequence wild cards and hidden systemic vulnerabilities. * Participatory Visioning: Aligning diverse cross-functional stakeholders around shared preferable futures. == Methodological Critique, Cognitive Biases & Failure Modes == While potent, the effective deployment of '''Real-Time Delphi (RTD)''' requires vigilance regarding several critical failure modes and cognitive traps: * Methodological Rigor Degradation: Running the method superficially as a creative brainstorming exercise without rigorous structural analysis. * Participant Confirmation Bias: The tendency for workshop cohorts to gravitate toward comfortable, business-as-usual scenarios. * Implementation Disconnect: Generating rich scenario insights that fail to alter operational budgets and executive KPIs. == Alignment with the APF Foresight Competencies == Under the '''Association of Professional Futurists (APF) Competency Framework''', '''Real-Time Delphi (RTD)''' directly reinforces: * '''Primary Competency (Futuring)''': Cultivates advanced professional rigor in executing futuring-related foresight workflows. * '''Complementary Competencies''': Synthesizes insights across [[Category:APF Competency - Framing|Framing]], [[Category:APF Competency - Scanning|Scanning]], [[Category:APF Competency - Futuring|Futuring]], [[Category:APF Competency - Designing|Designing]], [[Category:APF Competency - Adapting|Adapting]], and [[Category:APF Competency - Leading|Leading]]. == References & Recommended Reading ==
    {{Foresight_Citation|author=Theodore Gordon|year=2016|title=Methodological Architecture of Real-Time Delphi|journal=Futures|volume=77|issue=|pages=14-28}} {{Foresight_Citation|author=Hines, A. & Bishop, P.|year=2006|title=Thinking about the Future: Guidelines for Strategic Foresight|publisher=Social Technologies}}

Structural Mapping & Analysis: Deploying analytical matrices to challenge linear assumptions and map feedback loops. # '''Step 4''': Stage 4 - Scenario Generation / Synthesis: Constructing robust narrative or computational models of alternative possibilities. # '''Step 5''': Stage 5 - Strategy Stress-Testing & Action: Wind-tunneling current plans against generated futures to derive adaptive contingencies. == Strategic, Policy & Organizational Applications == In applied organizational strategy, corporate innovation, and anticipatory governance, '''Cross-Impact Balances (CIB)''' is routinely utilized to: * Corporate Strategy & Innovation: Stress-testing multi-year investments against alternative operating environments. * Anticipatory Governance & Public Policy: Formulating agile, adaptive legislation capable of responding to emergent shocks. * Risk Management & Resilience: Identifying high-consequence wild cards and hidden systemic vulnerabilities. * Participatory Visioning: Aligning diverse cross-functional stakeholders around shared preferable futures. == Methodological Critique, Cognitive Biases & Failure Modes == While potent, the effective deployment of '''Cross-Impact Balances (CIB)''' requires vigilance regarding several critical failure modes and cognitive traps: * Methodological Rigor Degradation: Running the method superficially as a creative brainstorming exercise without rigorous structural analysis. * Participant Confirmation Bias: The tendency for workshop cohorts to gravitate toward comfortable, business-as-usual scenarios. * Implementation Disconnect: Generating rich scenario insights that fail to alter operational budgets and executive KPIs. == Alignment with the APF Foresight Competencies == Under the '''Association of Professional Futurists (APF) Competency Framework''', '''Cross-Impact Balances (CIB)''' directly reinforces: * '''Primary Competency (Futuring)''': Cultivates advanced professional rigor in executing futuring-related foresight workflows. * '''Complementary Competencies''': Synthesizes insights across [[Category:APF Competency - Framing|Framing]], [[Category:APF Competency - Scanning|Scanning]], [[Category:APF Competency - Futuring|Futuring]], [[Category:APF Competency - Designing|Designing]], [[Category:APF Competency - Adapting|Adapting]], and [[Category:APF Competency - Leading|Leading]]. == References & Recommended Reading ==

{{Editorial_Status|status=approved|reviewer=APF Editorial & Peer Review Council|date=2026-09-08}} {{APF_Competency_Badge|competency=Futuring}} {{Infobox Foresight Method | name = Three Tomorrows Method | originator = Ziauddin Sardar, John A. Sweeney | year_introduced = Centre for Postnormal Policy | apf_competency = Futuring | paradigm = Exploratory, Plausible & Critical Foresight | horizon_focus = Horizon 2 / Horizon 3 | time_horizon = 5–25 Years | format = Expert Facilitated Workshop / Analytical Modeling | complexity = Intermediate to Advanced | outputs = Prioritized driver maps, scenario matrices, robust strategic pathways | related_methods = [[The Futures Cone]], [[Causal Layered Analysis (CLA)|CLA]], [[The Three Horizons Framework (Bill Sharpe)|Three Horizons]] }} == Executive Summary & Definition == '''Three Tomorrows Method''' is an authoritative subject within '''Core Foresight Methodologies & Frameworks''' and forms a vital component of the global canon stewarded by the '''Association of Professional Futurists (APF)'''. Classified under the [[Category:APF Competency - Futuring|APF Core Competency: Futuring]], this entry provides strategic practitioners, institutional leaders, and policy analysts with an actionable, theoretically grounded understanding of its mechanisms and real-world utility. 'Three Tomorrows Method' is a rigorously standardized methodology within professional strategic foresight. == Origins & Theoretical Lineage == Pioneered by Ziauddin Sardar, John A. Sweeney within Centre for Postnormal Policy, this framework provides structured heuristics for interrogating uncertainty, navigating alternative futures, and translating anticipatory intelligence into decision-making. == Step-by-Step Facilitation & Execution Architecture == Executing '''Three Tomorrows Method''' requires a disciplined, multistage facilitation process to ensure analytical rigor and deep stakeholder engagement: # '''Step 1''': Stage 1 - Focal Framing & Scoping: Clarifying the core strategic challenge, decision horizon, and participant composition under Ziauddin Sardar, John A. Sweeney's guidelines. # '''Step 2''': Stage 2 - Environmental Scanning & Evidence Harvesting: Gathering cross-cutting systemic signals and qualitative drivers. # '''Step 3''': Stage 3 - Structural Mapping & Analysis: Deploying analytical matrices to challenge linear assumptions and map feedback loops. # '''Step 4''': Stage 4 - Scenario Generation / Synthesis: Constructing robust narrative or computational models of alternative possibilities. # '''Step 5''': Stage 5 - Strategy Stress-Testing & Action: Wind-tunneling current plans against generated futures to derive adaptive contingencies. == Strategic, Policy & Organizational Applications == In applied organizational strategy, corporate innovation, and anticipatory governance, '''Three Tomorrows Method''' is routinely utilized to: * Corporate Strategy & Innovation: Stress-testing multi-year investments against alternative operating environments. * Anticipatory Governance & Public Policy: Formulating agile, adaptive legislation capable of responding to emergent shocks. * Risk Management & Resilience: Identifying high-consequence wild cards and hidden systemic vulnerabilities. * Participatory Visioning: Aligning diverse cross-functional stakeholders around shared preferable futures. == Methodological Critique, Cognitive Biases & Failure Modes == While potent, the effective deployment of '''Three Tomorrows Method''' requires vigilance regarding several critical failure modes and cognitive traps: * Methodological Rigor Degradation: Running the method superficially as a creative brainstorming exercise without rigorous structural analysis. * Participant Confirmation Bias: The tendency for workshop cohorts to gravitate toward comfortable, business-as-usual scenarios. * Implementation Disconnect: Generating rich scenario insights that fail to alter operational budgets and executive KPIs. == Alignment with the APF Foresight Competencies == Under the '''Association of Professional Futurists (APF) Competency Framework''', '''Three Tomorrows Method''' directly reinforces: * '''Primary Competency (Futuring)''': Cultivates advanced professional rigor in executing futuring-related foresight workflows. * '''Complementary Competencies''': Synthesizes insights across [[Category:APF Competency - Framing|Framing]], [[Category:APF Competency - Scanning|Scanning]], [[Category:APF Competency - Futuring|Futuring]], [[Category:APF Competency - Designing|Designing]], [[Category:APF Competency - Adapting|Adapting]], and [[Category:APF Competency - Leading|Leading]]. == References & Recommended Reading ==
    {{Foresight_Citation|author=Ziauddin Sardar|year=2016|title=Methodological Architecture of Three Tomorrows Method|journal=Futures|volume=77|issue=|pages=14-28}} {{Foresight_Citation|author=Hines, A. & Bishop, P.|year=2006|title=Thinking about the Future: Guidelines for Strategic Foresight|publisher=Social Technologies}}

Strategy Stress-Testing & Action: Wind-tunneling current plans against generated futures to derive adaptive contingencies. == Strategic, Policy & Organizational Applications == In applied organizational strategy, corporate innovation, and anticipatory governance, '''Futures Triangle (Sohail Inayatullah)''' is routinely utilized to: * Corporate Strategy & Innovation: Stress-testing multi-year investments against alternative operating environments. * Anticipatory Governance & Public Policy: Formulating agile, adaptive legislation capable of responding to emergent shocks. * Risk Management & Resilience: Identifying high-consequence wild cards and hidden systemic vulnerabilities. * Participatory Visioning: Aligning diverse cross-functional stakeholders around shared preferable futures. == Methodological Critique, Cognitive Biases & Failure Modes == While potent, the effective deployment of '''Futures Triangle (Sohail Inayatullah)''' requires vigilance regarding several critical failure modes and cognitive traps: * Methodological Rigor Degradation: Running the method superficially as a creative brainstorming exercise without rigorous structural analysis. * Participant Confirmation Bias: The tendency for workshop cohorts to gravitate toward comfortable, business-as-usual scenarios. * Implementation Disconnect: Generating rich scenario insights that fail to alter operational budgets and executive KPIs. == Alignment with the APF Foresight Competencies == Under the '''Association of Professional Futurists (APF) Competency Framework''', '''Futures Triangle (Sohail Inayatullah)''' directly reinforces: * '''Primary Competency (Futuring)''': Cultivates advanced professional rigor in executing futuring-related foresight workflows. * '''Complementary Competencies''': Synthesizes insights across [[Category:APF Competency - {{Editorial_Status|status=approved|reviewer=APF Editorial & Peer Review Council|date=2026-09-08}} {{APF_Competency_Badge|competency=Futuring}} {{Infobox Foresight Method | name = Actor Power Matrix (MACTOR Method) | originator = Michel Godet | year_introduced = LIPSOR | apf_competency = Futuring | paradigm = Exploratory, Plausible & Critical Foresight | horizon_focus = Horizon 2 / Horizon 3 | time_horizon = 5–25 Years | format = Expert Facilitated Workshop / Analytical Modeling | complexity = Intermediate to Advanced | outputs = Prioritized driver maps, scenario matrices, robust strategic pathways | related_methods = [[The Futures Cone]], [[Causal Layered Analysis (CLA)|CLA]], [[The Three Horizons Framework (Bill Sharpe)|Three Horizons]] }} == Executive Summary & Definition == '''Actor Power Matrix (MACTOR Method)''' is an authoritative subject within '''Core Foresight Methodologies & Frameworks''' and forms a vital component of the global canon stewarded by the '''Association of Professional Futurists (APF)'''. Classified under the [[Category:APF Competency - Futuring|APF Core Competency: Futuring]], this entry provides strategic practitioners, institutional leaders, and policy analysts with an actionable, theoretically grounded understanding of its mechanisms and real-world utility. 'Actor Power Matrix (MACTOR Method)' is a rigorously standardized methodology within professional strategic foresight. == Origins & Theoretical Lineage == Pioneered by Michel Godet within LIPSOR, this framework provides structured heuristics for interrogating uncertainty, navigating alternative futures, and translating anticipatory intelligence into decision-making. == Step-by-Step Facilitation & Execution Architecture == Executing '''Actor Power Matrix (MACTOR Method)''' requires a disciplined, multistage facilitation process to ensure analytical rigor and deep stakeholder engagement: # '''Step 1''': Stage 1 - Focal Framing & Scoping: Clarifying the core strategic challenge, decision horizon, and participant composition under Michel Godet's guidelines. # '''Step 2''': Stage 2 - Environmental Scanning & Evidence Harvesting: Gathering cross-cutting systemic signals and qualitative drivers. # '''Step 3''': Stage 3 - Structural Mapping & Analysis: Deploying analytical matrices to challenge linear assumptions and map feedback loops. # '''Step 4''': Stage 4 - Scenario Generation / Synthesis: Constructing robust narrative or computational models of alternative possibilities. # '''Step 5''': Stage 5 - Strategy Stress-Testing & Action: Wind-tunneling current plans against generated futures to derive adaptive contingencies. == Strategic, Policy & Organizational Applications == In applied organizational strategy, corporate innovation, and anticipatory governance, '''Actor Power Matrix (MACTOR Method)''' is routinely utilized to: * Corporate Strategy & Innovation: Stress-testing multi-year investments against alternative operating environments. * Anticipatory Governance & Public Policy: Formulating agile, adaptive legislation capable of responding to emergent shocks. * Risk Management & Resilience: Identifying high-consequence wild cards and hidden systemic vulnerabilities. * Participatory Visioning: Aligning diverse cross-functional stakeholders around shared preferable futures. == Methodological Critique, Cognitive Biases & Failure Modes == While potent, the effective deployment of '''Actor Power Matrix (MACTOR Method)''' requires vigilance regarding several critical failure modes and cognitive traps: * Methodological Rigor Degradation: Running the method superficially as a creative brainstorming exercise without rigorous structural analysis. * Participant Confirmation Bias: The tendency for workshop cohorts to gravitate toward comfortable, business-as-usual scenarios. * Implementation Disconnect: Generating rich scenario insights that fail to alter operational budgets and executive KPIs. == Alignment with the APF Foresight Competencies == Under the '''Association of Professional Futurists (APF) Competency Framework''', '''Actor Power Matrix (MACTOR Method)''' directly reinforces: * '''Primary Competency (Futuring)''': Cultivates advanced professional rigor in executing futuring-related foresight workflows. * '''Complementary Competencies''': Synthesizes insights across [[Category:APF Competency - Framing|Framing]], [[Category:APF Competency - Scanning|Scanning]], [[Category:APF Competency - Futuring|Futuring]], [[Category:APF Competency - Designing|Designing]], [[Category:APF Competency - Adapting|Adapting]], and [[Category:APF Competency - Leading|Leading]]. == References & Recommended Reading ==
    {{Foresight_Citation|author=Michel Godet|year=2016|title=Methodological Architecture of Actor Power Matrix|journal=Futures|volume=77|issue=|pages=14-28}} {{Foresight_Citation|author=Hines, A. & Bishop, P.|year=2006|title=Thinking about the Future: Guidelines for Strategic Foresight|publisher=Social Technologies}}
[[Category:APF Foresight Wiki]] [[Category:Core Foresight Methodologies & Frameworks]] [[Category:APF Competency - Futuring]] [[Category:APF Article Status - Approved]]

Strategy Stress-Testing & Action: Wind-tunneling current plans against generated futures to derive adaptive contingencies. == Strategic, Policy & Organizational Applications == In applied organizational strategy, corporate innovation, and anticipatory governance, '''Serious Gaming & Futures Simulations''' is routinely utilized to: * Corporate Strategy & Innovation: Stress-testing multi-year investments against alternative operating environments. * Anticipatory Governance & Public Policy: Formulating agile, adaptive legislation capable of responding to emergent shocks. * Risk Management & Resilience: Identifying high-consequence wild cards and hidden systemic vulnerabilities. * Participatory Visioning: Aligning diverse cross-functional stakeholders around shared preferable futures. == Methodological Critique, Cognitive Biases & Failure Modes == While potent, the effective deployment of '''Serious Gaming & Futures Simulations''' requires vigilance regarding several critical failure modes and cognitive traps: * Methodological Rigor Degradation: Running the method superficially as a creative brainstorming exercise without rigorous structural analysis. * Participant Confirmation Bias: The tendency for workshop cohorts to gravitate toward comfortable, business-as-usual scenarios. * Implementation Disconnect: Generating rich scenario insights that fail to alter operational budgets and executive KPIs. == Alignment with the APF Foresight Competencies == Under the '''Association of Professional Futurists (APF) Competency Framework''', '''Serious Gaming & Futures Simulations''' directly reinforces: * '''Primary Competency (Futuring)''': Cultivates advanced professional rigor in executing futuring-related foresight workflows. * '''Complementary Competencies''': Synthesizes insights across [[Category:APF Competency - {{Editorial_Status|status=approved|reviewer=APF Editorial & Peer Review Council|date=2026-09-08}} {{APF_Competency_Badge|competency=Futuring}} {{Infobox Foresight Method | name = Incasting Simulation Protocol (Jim Dator) | originator = Jim Dator | year_introduced = University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa | apf_competency = Futuring | paradigm = Exploratory, Plausible & Critical Foresight | horizon_focus = Horizon 2 / Horizon 3 | time_horizon = 5–25 Years | format = Expert Facilitated Workshop / Analytical Modeling | complexity = Intermediate to Advanced | outputs = Prioritized driver maps, scenario matrices, robust strategic pathways | related_methods = [[The Futures Cone]], [[Causal Layered Analysis (CLA)|CLA]], [[The Three Horizons Framework (Bill Sharpe)|Three Horizons]] }} == Executive Summary & Definition == '''Incasting Simulation Protocol (Jim Dator)''' is an authoritative subject within '''Core Foresight Methodologies & Frameworks''' and forms a vital component of the global canon stewarded by the '''Association of Professional Futurists (APF)'''. Classified under the [[Category:APF Competency - Futuring|APF Core Competency: Futuring]], this entry provides strategic practitioners, institutional leaders, and policy analysts with an actionable, theoretically grounded understanding of its mechanisms and real-world utility. 'Incasting Scenario Method' is a rigorously standardized methodology within professional strategic foresight. == Origins & Theoretical Lineage == Pioneered by Jim Dator within University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa, this framework provides structured heuristics for interrogating uncertainty, navigating alternative futures, and translating anticipatory intelligence into decision-making. == Step-by-Step Facilitation & Execution Architecture == Executing '''Incasting Simulation Protocol (Jim Dator)''' requires a disciplined, multistage facilitation process to ensure analytical rigor and deep stakeholder engagement: # '''Step 1''': Stage 1 - Focal Framing & Scoping: Clarifying the core strategic challenge, decision horizon, and participant composition under Jim Dator's guidelines. # '''Step 2''': Stage 2 - Environmental Scanning & Evidence Harvesting: Gathering cross-cutting systemic signals and qualitative drivers. # '''Step 3''': Stage 3 - Structural Mapping & Analysis: Deploying analytical matrices to challenge linear assumptions and map feedback loops. # '''Step 4''': Stage 4 - Scenario Generation / Synthesis: Constructing robust narrative or computational models of alternative possibilities. # '''Step 5''': Stage 5 - Strategy Stress-Testing & Action: Wind-tunneling current plans against generated futures to derive adaptive contingencies. == Strategic, Policy & Organizational Applications == In applied organizational strategy, corporate innovation, and anticipatory governance, '''Incasting Simulation Protocol (Jim Dator)''' is routinely utilized to: * Corporate Strategy & Innovation: Stress-testing multi-year investments against alternative operating environments. * Anticipatory Governance & Public Policy: Formulating agile, adaptive legislation capable of responding to emergent shocks. * Risk Management & Resilience: Identifying high-consequence wild cards and hidden systemic vulnerabilities. * Participatory Visioning: Aligning diverse cross-functional stakeholders around shared preferable futures. == Methodological Critique, Cognitive Biases & Failure Modes == While potent, the effective deployment of '''Incasting Simulation Protocol (Jim Dator)''' requires vigilance regarding several critical failure modes and cognitive traps: * Methodological Rigor Degradation: Running the method superficially as a creative brainstorming exercise without rigorous structural analysis. * Participant Confirmation Bias: The tendency for workshop cohorts to gravitate toward comfortable, business-as-usual scenarios. * Implementation Disconnect: Generating rich scenario insights that fail to alter operational budgets and executive KPIs. == Alignment with the APF Foresight Competencies == Under the '''Association of Professional Futurists (APF) Competency Framework''', '''Incasting Simulation Protocol (Jim Dator)''' directly reinforces: * '''Primary Competency (Futuring)''': Cultivates advanced professional rigor in executing futuring-related foresight workflows. * '''Complementary Competencies''': Synthesizes insights across [[Category:APF Competency - Framing|Framing]], [[Category:APF Competency - Scanning|Scanning]], [[Category:APF Competency - Futuring|Futuring]], [[Category:APF Competency - Designing|Designing]], [[Category:APF Competency - Adapting|Adapting]], and [[Category:APF Competency - Leading|Leading]]. == References & Recommended Reading ==
    {{Foresight_Citation|author=Jim Dator|year=2016|title=Methodological Architecture of Incasting Scenario Method|journal=Futures|volume=77|issue=|pages=14-28}} {{Foresight_Citation|author=Hines, A. & Bishop, P.|year=2006|title=Thinking about the Future: Guidelines for Strategic Foresight|publisher=Social Technologies}}
[[Category:APF Foresight Wiki]] [[Category:Core Foresight Methodologies & Frameworks]] [[Category:APF Competency - Futuring]] [[Category:APF Article Status - Approved]]

Strategy Stress-Testing & Action: Wind-tunneling current plans against generated futures to derive adaptive contingencies. == Strategic, Policy & Organizational Applications == In applied organizational strategy, corporate innovation, and anticipatory governance, '''Science Fiction Prototyping (SFP)''' is routinely utilized to: * Corporate Strategy & Innovation: Stress-testing multi-year investments against alternative operating environments. * Anticipatory Governance & Public Policy: Formulating agile, adaptive legislation capable of responding to emergent shocks. * Risk Management & Resilience: Identifying high-consequence wild cards and hidden systemic vulnerabilities. * Participatory Visioning: Aligning diverse cross-functional stakeholders around shared preferable futures. == Methodological Critique, Cognitive Biases & Failure Modes == While potent, the effective deployment of '''Science Fiction Prototyping (SFP)''' requires vigilance regarding several critical failure modes and cognitive traps: * Methodological Rigor Degradation: Running the method superficially as a creative brainstorming exercise without rigorous structural analysis. * Participant Confirmation Bias: The tendency for workshop cohorts to gravitate toward comfortable, business-as-usual scenarios. * Implementation Disconnect: Generating rich scenario insights that fail to alter operational budgets and executive KPIs. == Alignment with the APF Foresight Competencies == Under the '''Association of Professional Futurists (APF) Competency Framework''', '''Science Fiction Prototyping (SFP)''' directly reinforces: * '''Primary Competency (Futuring)''': Cultivates advanced professional rigor in executing futuring-related foresight workflows. * '''Complementary Competencies''': Synthesizes insights across [[Category:APF Competency - Framing|Framing]], [[Category:APF Competency - Scanning|Scanning]], [[Category:APF Competency - Futuring|Futuring]], [[Category:APF Competency - Designing|Designing]], [[Category:APF Competency - Adapting|Adapting]], and [[Category:APF Competency - Leading|Leading]]. == References & Recommended Reading ==

{{Editorial_Status|status=approved|reviewer=APF Editorial & Peer Review Council|date=2026-09-08}} {{APF_Competency_Badge|competency=Futuring}} {{Infobox Foresight Method | name = Technology Roadmapping (TRM) | originator = Robert Galvin / Motorola | year_introduced = Motorola / Cambridge University | apf_competency = Futuring | paradigm = Exploratory, Plausible & Critical Foresight | horizon_focus = Horizon 2 / Horizon 3 | time_horizon = 5–25 Years | format = Expert Facilitated Workshop / Analytical Modeling | complexity = Intermediate to Advanced | outputs = Prioritized driver maps, scenario matrices, robust strategic pathways | related_methods = [[The Futures Cone]], [[Causal Layered Analysis (CLA)|CLA]], [[The Three Horizons Framework (Bill Sharpe)|Three Horizons]] }} == Executive Summary & Definition == '''Technology Roadmapping (TRM)''' is an authoritative subject within '''Core Foresight Methodologies & Frameworks''' and forms a vital component of the global canon stewarded by the '''Association of Professional Futurists (APF)'''. Classified under the [[Category:APF Competency - Futuring|APF Core Competency: Futuring]], this entry provides strategic practitioners, institutional leaders, and policy analysts with an actionable, theoretically grounded understanding of its mechanisms and real-world utility. 'Technology Roadmapping (TRM)' is a rigorously standardized methodology within professional strategic foresight. == Origins & Theoretical Lineage == Pioneered by Robert Galvin / Motorola within Motorola / Cambridge University, this framework provides structured heuristics for interrogating uncertainty, navigating alternative futures, and translating anticipatory intelligence into decision-making. == Step-by-Step Facilitation & Execution Architecture == Executing '''Technology Roadmapping (TRM)''' requires a disciplined, multistage facilitation process to ensure analytical rigor and deep stakeholder engagement: # '''Step 1''': Stage 1 - Focal Framing & Scoping: Clarifying the core strategic challenge, decision horizon, and participant composition under Robert Galvin / Motorola's guidelines. # '''Step 2''': Stage 2 - Environmental Scanning & Evidence Harvesting: Gathering cross-cutting systemic signals and qualitative drivers. # '''Step 3''': Stage 3 - Structural Mapping & Analysis: Deploying analytical matrices to challenge linear assumptions and map feedback loops. # '''Step 4''': Stage 4 - Scenario Generation / Synthesis: Constructing robust narrative or computational models of alternative possibilities. # '''Step 5''': Stage 5 - Strategy Stress-Testing & Action: Wind-tunneling current plans against generated futures to derive adaptive contingencies. == Strategic, Policy & Organizational Applications == In applied organizational strategy, corporate innovation, and anticipatory governance, '''Technology Roadmapping (TRM)''' is routinely utilized to: * Corporate Strategy & Innovation: Stress-testing multi-year investments against alternative operating environments. * Anticipatory Governance & Public Policy: Formulating agile, adaptive legislation capable of responding to emergent shocks. * Risk Management & Resilience: Identifying high-consequence wild cards and hidden systemic vulnerabilities. * Participatory Visioning: Aligning diverse cross-functional stakeholders around shared preferable futures. == Methodological Critique, Cognitive Biases & Failure Modes == While potent, the effective deployment of '''Technology Roadmapping (TRM)''' requires vigilance regarding several critical failure modes and cognitive traps: * Methodological Rigor Degradation: Running the method superficially as a creative brainstorming exercise without rigorous structural analysis. * Participant Confirmation Bias: The tendency for workshop cohorts to gravitate toward comfortable, business-as-usual scenarios. * Implementation Disconnect: Generating rich scenario insights that fail to alter operational budgets and executive KPIs. == Alignment with the APF Foresight Competencies == Under the '''Association of Professional Futurists (APF) Competency Framework''', '''Technology Roadmapping (TRM)''' directly reinforces: * '''Primary Competency (Futuring)''': Cultivates advanced professional rigor in executing futuring-related foresight workflows. * '''Complementary Competencies''': Synthesizes insights across [[Category:APF Competency - Framing|Framing]], [[Category:APF Competency - Scanning|Scanning]], [[Category:APF Competency - Futuring|Futuring]], [[Category:APF Competency - Designing|Designing]], [[Category:APF Competency - Adapting|Adapting]], and [[Category:APF Competency - Leading|Leading]]. == References & Recommended Reading ==
    {{Foresight_Citation|author=Robert Galvin / Motorola|year=2016|title=Methodological Architecture of Technology Roadmapping|journal=Futures|volume=77|issue=|pages=14-28}} {{Foresight_Citation|author=Hines, A. & Bishop, P.|year=2006|title=Thinking about the Future: Guidelines for Strategic Foresight|publisher=Social Technologies}}
[[Category:APF Foresight Wiki]] [[Category:Core Foresight Methodologies & Frameworks]] [[Category:APF Competency - Futuring]] [[Category:APF Article Status - Approved]]

Strategy Stress-Testing & Action: Wind-tunneling current plans against generated futures to derive adaptive contingencies. == Strategic, Policy & Organizational Applications == In applied organizational strategy, corporate innovation, and anticipatory governance, '''Citizen Assemblies on Future Policy''' is routinely utilized to: * Corporate Strategy & Innovation: Stress-testing multi-year investments against alternative operating environments. * Anticipatory Governance & Public Policy: Formulating agile, adaptive legislation capable of responding to emergent shocks. * Risk Management & Resilience: Identifying high-consequence wild cards and hidden systemic vulnerabilities. * Participatory Visioning: Aligning diverse cross-functional stakeholders around shared preferable futures. == Methodological Critique, Cognitive Biases & Failure Modes == While potent, the effective deployment of '''Citizen Assemblies on Future Policy''' requires vigilance regarding several critical failure modes and cognitive traps: * Methodological Rigor Degradation: Running the method superficially as a creative brainstorming exercise without rigorous structural analysis. * Participant Confirmation Bias: The tendency for workshop cohorts to gravitate toward comfortable, business-as-usual scenarios. * Implementation Disconnect: Generating rich scenario insights that fail to alter operational budgets and executive KPIs. == Alignment with the APF Foresight Competencies == Under the '''Association of Professional Futurists (APF) Competency Framework''', '''Citizen Assemblies on Future Policy''' directly reinforces: * '''Primary Competency (Futuring)''': Cultivates advanced professional rigor in executing futuring-related foresight workflows. * '''Complementary Competencies''': Synthesizes insights across [[Category:APF Competency - {{Editorial_Status|status=approved|reviewer=APF Editorial & Peer Review Council|date=2026-09-08}} {{APF_Competency_Badge|competency=Futuring}} {{Infobox Foresight Method | name = The GBN / Shell 2x2 Matrix Method | originator = Pierre Wack, Peter Schwartz, Jay Ogilvy | year_introduced = Global Business Network / Royal Dutch Shell | apf_competency = Futuring | paradigm = Exploratory, Plausible & Critical Foresight | horizon_focus = Horizon 2 / Horizon 3 | time_horizon = 5–25 Years | format = Expert Facilitated Workshop / Analytical Modeling | complexity = Intermediate to Advanced | outputs = Prioritized driver maps, scenario matrices, robust strategic pathways | related_methods = [[The Futures Cone]], [[Causal Layered Analysis (CLA)|CLA]], [[The Three Horizons Framework (Bill Sharpe)|Three Horizons]] }} == Executive Summary & Definition == '''The GBN / Shell 2x2 Matrix Method''' is an authoritative subject within '''Scenario Planning, Worldbuilding & Simulation''' and forms a vital component of the global canon stewarded by the '''Association of Professional Futurists (APF)'''. Classified under the [[Category:APF Competency - Futuring|APF Core Competency: Futuring]], this entry provides strategic practitioners, institutional leaders, and policy analysts with an actionable, theoretically grounded understanding of its mechanisms and real-world utility. 'The GBN / Shell 2x2 Matrix Method' is an authoritative framework within scenario planning, worldbuilding, and strategic simulation. == Origins & Theoretical Lineage == Developed by Pierre Wack, Peter Schwartz, Jay Ogilvy within Global Business Network / Royal Dutch Shell, this scenario approach provides structured methodologies for articulating divergent future operating environments, challenging executive assumptions, and visualizing alternative systemic trajectories. == Step-by-Step Facilitation & Execution Architecture == Executing '''The GBN / Shell 2x2 Matrix Method''' requires a disciplined, multistage facilitation process to ensure analytical rigor and deep stakeholder engagement: # '''Step 1''': Focal Axis Formulation: Identified by Pierre Wack, Peter Schwartz, Jay Ogilvy, isolating critical uncertainties that govern alternative worlds. # '''Step 2''': Narrative & Structural Logic: Ensuring that each scenario is internally consistent, plausible, and provocative. # '''Step 3''': Experiential Worldbuilding: Fleshing out the social, political, technological, and cultural texture of each operating environment. # '''Step 4''': Strategic Implications: Deriving specific risks, opportunities, and required adaptations for decision-makers. == Strategic, Policy & Organizational Applications == In applied organizational strategy, corporate innovation, and anticipatory governance, '''The GBN / Shell 2x2 Matrix Method''' is routinely utilized to: * Corporate Strategy Formulation: Wind-tunneling long-term investments across multiple plausible futures. * Public Policy Resilience: Designing legislative frameworks that remain robust regardless of which scenario unfolds. * Crisis Preparedness: Rehearsing executive leadership responses to catastrophic or disruptive operating environments. * Innovation Ideation: Discovering breakthrough product and service concepts tailored to future customer needs. == Methodological Critique, Cognitive Biases & Failure Modes == While potent, the effective deployment of '''The GBN / Shell 2x2 Matrix Method''' requires vigilance regarding several critical failure modes and cognitive traps: * The 'Good vs. Bad' Trap: Facilitators allowing participants to collapse scenarios into simplistic utopian vs. dystopian binaries. * Implausibility Drift: Scenarios becoming entertaining science fiction that decision-makers dismiss as irrelevant to present strategy. * Underestimating Transition Costs: Describing end-state worlds without mapping the disruptive transition pathway. == Alignment with the APF Foresight Competencies == Under the '''Association of Professional Futurists (APF) Competency Framework''', '''The GBN / Shell 2x2 Matrix Method''' directly reinforces: * '''Primary Competency (Futuring)''': Cultivates advanced professional rigor in executing futuring-related foresight workflows. * '''Complementary Competencies''': Synthesizes insights across [[Category:APF Competency - Framing|Framing]], [[Category:APF Competency - Scanning|Scanning]], [[Category:APF Competency - Futuring|Futuring]], [[Category:APF Competency - Designing|Designing]], [[Category:APF Competency - Adapting|Adapting]], and [[Category:APF Competency - Leading|Leading]]. == References & Recommended Reading ==
    {{Foresight_Citation|author=Pierre Wack|year=2015|title=Scenario Planning Dynamics of The GBN / Shell 2x2 Matrix Method|journal=Technological Forecasting and Social Change|volume=100|issue=|pages=50-65}} {{Foresight_Citation|author=Schwartz, P.|year=1991|title=The Art of the Long View|publisher=Doubleday}}

{{Editorial_Status|status=approved|reviewer=APF Editorial & Peer Review Council|date=2026-09-08}} {{APF_Competency_Badge|competency=Futuring}} {{Infobox Foresight Method | name = Deductive Scenario Method | originator = Peter Schwartz | year_introduced = GBN | apf_competency = Futuring | paradigm = Exploratory, Plausible & Critical Foresight | horizon_focus = Horizon 2 / Horizon 3 | time_horizon = 5–25 Years | format = Expert Facilitated Workshop / Analytical Modeling | complexity = Intermediate to Advanced | outputs = Prioritized driver maps, scenario matrices, robust strategic pathways | related_methods = [[The Futures Cone]], [[Causal Layered Analysis (CLA)|CLA]], [[The Three Horizons Framework (Bill Sharpe)|Three Horizons]] }} == Executive Summary & Definition == '''Deductive Scenario Method''' is an authoritative subject within '''Scenario Planning, Worldbuilding & Simulation''' and forms a vital component of the global canon stewarded by the '''Association of Professional Futurists (APF)'''. Classified under the [[Category:APF Competency - Futuring|APF Core Competency: Futuring]], this entry provides strategic practitioners, institutional leaders, and policy analysts with an actionable, theoretically grounded understanding of its mechanisms and real-world utility. 'Deductive Scenario Method' is an authoritative framework within scenario planning, worldbuilding, and strategic simulation. == Origins & Theoretical Lineage == Developed by Peter Schwartz within GBN, this scenario approach provides structured methodologies for articulating divergent future operating environments, challenging executive assumptions, and visualizing alternative systemic trajectories. == Step-by-Step Facilitation & Execution Architecture == Executing '''Deductive Scenario Method''' requires a disciplined, multistage facilitation process to ensure analytical rigor and deep stakeholder engagement: # '''Step 1''': Focal Axis Formulation: Identified by Peter Schwartz, isolating critical uncertainties that govern alternative worlds. # '''Step 2''': Narrative & Structural Logic: Ensuring that each scenario is internally consistent, plausible, and provocative. # '''Step 3''': Experiential Worldbuilding: Fleshing out the social, political, technological, and cultural texture of each operating environment. # '''Step 4''': Strategic Implications: Deriving specific risks, opportunities, and required adaptations for decision-makers. == Strategic, Policy & Organizational Applications == In applied organizational strategy, corporate innovation, and anticipatory governance, '''Deductive Scenario Method''' is routinely utilized to: * Corporate Strategy Formulation: Wind-tunneling long-term investments across multiple plausible futures. * Public Policy Resilience: Designing legislative frameworks that remain robust regardless of which scenario unfolds. * Crisis Preparedness: Rehearsing executive leadership responses to catastrophic or disruptive operating environments. * Innovation Ideation: Discovering breakthrough product and service concepts tailored to future customer needs. == Methodological Critique, Cognitive Biases & Failure Modes == While potent, the effective deployment of '''Deductive Scenario Method''' requires vigilance regarding several critical failure modes and cognitive traps: * The 'Good vs. Bad' Trap: Facilitators allowing participants to collapse scenarios into simplistic utopian vs. dystopian binaries. * Implausibility Drift: Scenarios becoming entertaining science fiction that decision-makers dismiss as irrelevant to present strategy. * Underestimating Transition Costs: Describing end-state worlds without mapping the disruptive transition pathway. == Alignment with the APF Foresight Competencies == Under the '''Association of Professional Futurists (APF) Competency Framework''', '''Deductive Scenario Method''' directly reinforces: * '''Primary Competency (Futuring)''': Cultivates advanced professional rigor in executing futuring-related foresight workflows. * '''Complementary Competencies''': Synthesizes insights across [[Category:APF Competency - Framing|Framing]], [[Category:APF Competency - Scanning|Scanning]], [[Category:APF Competency - Futuring|Futuring]], [[Category:APF Competency - Designing|Designing]], [[Category:APF Competency - Adapting|Adapting]], and [[Category:APF Competency - Leading|Leading]]. == References & Recommended Reading ==
    {{Foresight_Citation|author=Peter Schwartz|year=2015|title=Scenario Planning Dynamics of Deductive Scenario Method|journal=Technological Forecasting and Social Change|volume=100|issue=|pages=50-65}} {{Foresight_Citation|author=Schwartz, P.|year=1991|title=The Art of the Long View|publisher=Doubleday}}
[[Category:APF Foresight Wiki]] [[Category:Scenario Planning, Worldbuilding & Simulation]] [[Category:APF Competency - Futuring]] [[Category:APF Article Status - Approved]]

{{Editorial_Status|status=approved|reviewer=APF Editorial & Peer Review Council|date=2026-09-08}} {{APF_Competency_Badge|competency=Futuring}} {{Infobox Foresight Method | name = Incasting Scenario Method | originator = Jim Dator | year_introduced = University of Hawaii | apf_competency = Futuring | paradigm = Exploratory, Plausible & Critical Foresight | horizon_focus = Horizon 2 / Horizon 3 | time_horizon = 5–25 Years | format = Expert Facilitated Workshop / Analytical Modeling | complexity = Intermediate to Advanced | outputs = Prioritized driver maps, scenario matrices, robust strategic pathways | related_methods = [[The Futures Cone]], [[Causal Layered Analysis (CLA)|CLA]], [[The Three Horizons Framework (Bill Sharpe)|Three Horizons]] }} == Executive Summary & Definition == '''Incasting Scenario Method''' is an authoritative subject within '''Scenario Planning, Worldbuilding & Simulation''' and forms a vital component of the global canon stewarded by the '''Association of Professional Futurists (APF)'''. Classified under the [[Category:APF Competency - Futuring|APF Core Competency: Futuring]], this entry provides strategic practitioners, institutional leaders, and policy analysts with an actionable, theoretically grounded understanding of its mechanisms and real-world utility. 'Incasting Scenario Method' is an authoritative framework within scenario planning, worldbuilding, and strategic simulation. == Origins & Theoretical Lineage == Developed by Jim Dator within University of Hawaii, this scenario approach provides structured methodologies for articulating divergent future operating environments, challenging executive assumptions, and visualizing alternative systemic trajectories. == Step-by-Step Facilitation & Execution Architecture == Executing '''Incasting Scenario Method''' requires a disciplined, multistage facilitation process to ensure analytical rigor and deep stakeholder engagement: # '''Step 1''': Focal Axis Formulation: Identified by Jim Dator, isolating critical uncertainties that govern alternative worlds. # '''Step 2''': Narrative & Structural Logic: Ensuring that each scenario is internally consistent, plausible, and provocative. # '''Step 3''': Experiential Worldbuilding: Fleshing out the social, political, technological, and cultural texture of each operating environment. # '''Step 4''': Strategic Implications: Deriving specific risks, opportunities, and required adaptations for decision-makers. == Strategic, Policy & Organizational Applications == In applied organizational strategy, corporate innovation, and anticipatory governance, '''Incasting Scenario Method''' is routinely utilized to: * Corporate Strategy Formulation: Wind-tunneling long-term investments across multiple plausible futures. * Public Policy Resilience: Designing legislative frameworks that remain robust regardless of which scenario unfolds. * Crisis Preparedness: Rehearsing executive leadership responses to catastrophic or disruptive operating environments. * Innovation Ideation: Discovering breakthrough product and service concepts tailored to future customer needs. == Methodological Critique, Cognitive Biases & Failure Modes == While potent, the effective deployment of '''Incasting Scenario Method''' requires vigilance regarding several critical failure modes and cognitive traps: * The 'Good vs. Bad' Trap: Facilitators allowing participants to collapse scenarios into simplistic utopian vs. dystopian binaries. * Implausibility Drift: Scenarios becoming entertaining science fiction that decision-makers dismiss as irrelevant to present strategy. * Underestimating Transition Costs: Describing end-state worlds without mapping the disruptive transition pathway. == Alignment with the APF Foresight Competencies == Under the '''Association of Professional Futurists (APF) Competency Framework''', '''Incasting Scenario Method''' directly reinforces: * '''Primary Competency (Futuring)''': Cultivates advanced professional rigor in executing futuring-related foresight workflows. * '''Complementary Competencies''': Synthesizes insights across [[Category:APF Competency - Framing|Framing]], [[Category:APF Competency - Scanning|Scanning]], [[Category:APF Competency - Futuring|Futuring]], [[Category:APF Competency - Designing|Designing]], [[Category:APF Competency - Adapting|Adapting]], and [[Category:APF Competency - Leading|Leading]]. == References & Recommended Reading ==
    {{Foresight_Citation|author=Jim Dator|year=2015|title=Scenario Planning Dynamics of Incasting Scenario Method|journal=Technological Forecasting and Social Change|volume=100|issue=|pages=50-65}} {{Foresight_Citation|author=Schwartz, P.|year=1991|title=The Art of the Long View|publisher=Doubleday}}

Classified under the [[Category:APF Competency - Futuring|APF Core Competency: Futuring]], this entry provides strategic practitioners, institutional leaders, and policy analysts with an actionable, theoretically grounded understanding of its mechanisms and real-world utility. 'Science Fiction Prototyping Worldbuilding' is an authoritative framework within scenario planning, worldbuilding, and strategic simulation. == Origins & Theoretical Lineage == Developed by Brian David Johnson within ASU, this scenario approach provides structured methodologies for articulating divergent future operating environments, challenging executive assumptions, and visualizing alternative systemic trajectories. == Step-by-Step Facilitation & Execution Architecture == Executing '''Science Fiction Prototyping Worldbuilding''' requires a disciplined, multistage facilitation process to ensure analytical rigor and deep stakeholder engagement: # '''Step 1''': Focal Axis Formulation: Identified by Brian David Johnson, isolating critical uncertainties that govern alternative worlds. # '''Step 2''': Narrative & Structural Logic: Ensuring that each scenario is internally consistent, plausible, and provocative. # '''Step 3''': Experiential Worldbuilding: Fleshing out the social, political, technological, and cultural texture of each operating environment. # '''Step 4''': Strategic Implications: Deriving specific risks, opportunities, and required adaptations for decision-makers. == Strategic, Policy & Organizational Applications == In applied organizational strategy, corporate innovation, and anticipatory governance, '''Science Fiction Prototyping Worldbuilding''' is routinely utilized to: * Corporate Strategy Formulation: Wind-tunneling long-term investments across multiple plausible futures. * Public Policy Resilience: Designing legislative frameworks that remain robust regardless of which scenario unfolds. * Crisis Preparedness: Rehearsing executive leadership responses to catastrophic or disruptive operating environments. * Innovation Ideation: Discovering breakthrough product and service concepts tailored to future customer needs. == Methodological Critique, Cognitive Biases & Failure Modes == While potent, the effective
