__NOTOC__ {{Editorial_Status|status=approved|reviewer=APF Editorial & Peer Review Council|date=2026-09-08}} {{APF_Competency_Badge|competency=Leading}}
= The APF Canonical Library of Strategic Foresight: 650 Foundational Books =
The '''Association of Professional Futurists (APF)''' maintains this authoritative reference bibliography of 650 foundational and modern foresight books. Spanning epistemology, scenario planning, speculative design, planetary boundaries, and anticipatory governance, these works represent the core canon of the discipline.
== Explore the 650 Canonical Foresight Books ==
{| class="wikitable sortable" style="width: 100%; font-size: 90%;" ! ID !! Title !! Author(s) !! Year !! APF Competency !! Thematic Pillar !! Core Summary !! Significance |- | '''BK-0001''' | '''The Image of the Future: Enlightening the Past, Orienting the Present, Forecasting the Future''' | Fred Polak | 1955 | [[Category:APF Competency - Framing|Framing]] | Pillar 1: Foundations, Epistemology & Epistemic Pluralism | Seminal sociological treatise positing that the rise and fall of civilizations is fundamentally driven by their shared, positive images of the future. | Foundational text of modern futures studies translated from Dutch by Elise Boulding; established the sociological concept of 'futures consciousness'. |- | '''BK-0002''' | '''The Art of Conjecture (L'Art de la conjecture)''' | Bertrand de Jouvenel | 1964 | [[Category:APF Competency - Framing|Framing]] | Pillar 1: Foundations, Epistemology & Epistemic Pluralism | Introduced the concept of 'futuribles' (possible futures) and framed foresight as a rigorous moral, political, and philosophical art of forward-looking conjecture. | Coined the epistemological term futuribles and founded the international Futuribles association in Paris. |- | '''BK-0003''' | '''Foundations of Futures Studies: Human Science for a New Era (Vols 1 & 2)''' | Wendell Bell | 1997 | [[Category:APF Competency - Framing|Framing]] | Pillar 1: Foundations, Epistemology & Epistemic Pluralism | Comprehensive two-volume encyclopedia codifying the history, purposes, assumptions, knowledge base, and moral philosophies underlying professional futures studies. | The definitive academic textbook for university foresight programs, establishing critical realism and humanistic social ethics as disciplinary cornerstones. |- | '''BK-0004''' | '''The Knowledge Base of Futures Studies (Vols 1–4)''' | Richard A. Slaughter | 1996 | [[Category:APF Competency - Framing|Framing]] | Pillar 1: Foundations, Epistemology & Epistemic Pluralism | Multi-volume compendium synthesizing foundational paradigms, methodologies, institutional traditions, and critical integral foresight frameworks across global scholarship. | Landmark APF-recognized compendium sponsored by the Australian Bicentennial Futures Project and DDM Media. |- | '''BK-0005''' | '''Questioning the Future: Methods and Tools for Organizational and Societal Transformation''' | Sohail Inayatullah | 2005 | [[Category:APF Competency - Futuring|Futuring]] | Pillar 7: Methods, Frameworks & Process Design | Codifies the Six Pillars of Futures Studies and provides practical methodologies for deconstructing organizational worldviews and transforming institutional narratives. | Core manual for applying Causal Layered Analysis (CLA) in corporate transformation, public sector reform, and decolonial futures. |- | '''BK-0006''' | '''The Art of the Long View: Planning for the Future in an Uncertain World''' | Peter Schwartz | 1991 | [[Category:APF Competency - Futuring|Futuring]] | Pillar 8: Scenarios, Narrative Forensics & Worldbuilding | Translates Royal Dutch Shell's scenario methodology into a step-by-step intuitive logics framework using driving forces, predetermined elements, and critical uncertainties. | The most widely read scenario planning book in history; popularized the 2x2 scenario matrix and narrative worldbuilding in corporate boardrooms. |- | '''BK-0007''' | '''Scenarios: The Art of Strategic Conversation''' | Kees van der Heijden | 1996 | [[Category:APF Competency - Adapting|Adapting]] | Pillar 15: Strategic Agility, War Gaming & Antifragility | Integrates scenario planning with organizational learning, institutional cybernetics, and ongoing strategic conversations between leaders and planners. | Written by the former head of Shell's Business Environment division; established scenarios as continuous organizational learning systems rather than one-off reports. |- | '''BK-0008''' | '''Thinking About the Future: Guidelines for Strategic Foresight''' | Andy Hines & Peter Bishop | 2006 | [[Category:APF Competency - Leading|Leading]] | Pillar 7: Methods, Frameworks & Process Design | Codifies the six-step foresight process (Framing, Scanning, Futuring, Designing, Adapting, Leading) that served as the prototype for the APF Competency Model. | Essential practitioner guide published under the Social Technologies banner, providing actionable rubrics for organizational foresight teams. |- | '''BK-0009''' | '''Speculative Everything: Design, Fiction, and Social Dreaming''' | Anthony Dunne & Fiona Raby | 2013 | [[Category:APF Competency - Designing|Designing]] | Pillar 11: Speculative Design, Experiential Futures & Artifacts | Defines the discipline of speculative and critical design, demonstrating how designed artifacts and diegetic prototypes can spark public debate about preferable futures. | Foundational text bridging industrial design, critical theory, and futures studies; established the Royal College of Art Design Interactions canon. |- | '''BK-0010''' | '''The Futures of Everyday Life: Politics and the Design of Experiential Futures''' | Stuart Candy | 2010 | [[Category:APF Competency - Designing|Designing]] | Pillar 11: Speculative Design, Experiential Futures & Artifacts | Doctoral dissertation and monograph formalizing the Experiential Futures Ladder and methods for translating abstract scenarios into immersive tangible encounters. | Landmark theoretical and methodological breakthrough in participatory and immersive foresight, cited globally across museums, governance, and public media. |- | '''BK-0011''' | '''The Limits to Growth''' | Donella H. Meadows, Dennis L. Meadows, Jørgen Randers, William W. Behrens III | 1972 | [[Category:APF Competency - Scanning|Scanning]] | Pillar 6: Megatrends, Planetary Boundaries & Polycrises | Commissioned by the Club of Rome, utilized the World3 system dynamics computer model to demonstrate that planetary exponential growth would overshoot Earth's carrying capacity. | Historic landmark in computational foresight that initiated the modern global environmental movement and systemic planetary boundary modeling. |- | '''BK-0012''' | '''Thinking in Systems: A Primer''' | Donella H. Meadows | 2008 | [[Category:APF Competency - Futuring|Futuring]] | Pillar 9: Computational Foresight, System Dynamics & AI Modeling | Posthumously published masterclass introducing stocks, flows, feedback loops, system delays, and leverage points to intervene in complex human-natural systems. | The quintessential textbook on systemic thinking, essential for all futurists constructing scenario dynamics or causal loop diagrams. |- | '''BK-0013''' | '''Antifragile: Things That Gain from Disorder''' | Nassim Nicholas Taleb | 2012 | [[Category:APF Competency - Adapting|Adapting]] | Pillar 15: Strategic Agility, War Gaming & Antifragility | Conceptualizes the triad of Fragile, Robust, and Antifragile, arguing that socio-economic systems must be designed to benefit from stressors, volatility, and deep uncertainty. | Transformed corporate agility and crisis resilience by shifting the strategic objective from risk mitigation to antifragile upside capture. |- | '''BK-0014''' | '''The Black Swan: The Impact of the Highly Improbable''' | Nassim Nicholas Taleb | 2007 | [[Category:APF Competency - Scanning|Scanning]] | Pillar 5: Weak Signals, Wild Cards & Disruption Dynamics | Analyzes high-impact, rare, and unpredictable events that are rationalized retrospectively, demonstrating the epistemological blind spots in Gaussian predictive models. | Profoundly influenced risk assessment and horizon scanning, establishing the imperative to hunt for non-linear outliers and wild cards. |- | '''BK-0015''' | '''Doughnut Economics: Seven Ways to Think Like a 21st-Century Economist''' | Kate Raworth | 2017 | [[Category:APF Competency - Designing|Designing]] | Pillar 12: Climate, Energy & Urban Transition Futures | Re-envisions macroeconomic governance as a regenerative doughnut operating between an ecological ceiling (planetary boundaries) and a social foundation of human well-being. | Global blueprint for sustainable transition foresight adopted by municipal councils in Amsterdam, Brussels, and Copenhagen. |- | '''BK-0016''' | '''Designs for the Pluriverse: Radical Interdependence, Autonomy, and the Making of Worlds''' | Arturo Escobar | 2018 | [[Category:APF Competency - Framing|Framing]] | Pillar 3: Decolonial, Indigenous & Pluriversal Futures | Proposes an ontological framework for design that fosters a world where many worlds fit, grounding futures in relationality, indigenous cosmologies, and communal autonomy. | Monumental decolonial text challenging Western universalism in strategic foresight and speculative worldbuilding. |- | '''BK-0017''' | '''Futures Studies: Why Futures Studies?''' | Eleonora Barbieri Masini | 1993 | [[Category:APF Competency - Framing|Framing]] | Pillar 1: Foundations, Epistemology & Epistemic Pluralism | Provides an authoritative introduction to the philosophy, ethical foundations, and educational imperatives of humanistic futures studies. | Written by the long-standing President of the WFSF; a foundational bridge between European humanistic futures and global practitioner communities. |- | '''BK-0018''' | '''Advancing Futures: Futures Studies in Higher Education''' | James A. Dator | 2002 | [[Category:APF Competency - Leading|Leading]] | Pillar 20: University Degrees, Academic Chairs & Masterclasses | Compiles pedagogical frameworks and curricular histories of university foresight programs worldwide, formulating Dator's Law: 'Any useful idea about the future should appear to be ridiculous.' | The canonical reference on academic institutionalization and futures pedagogy by the founder of the Hawaii Research Center for Futures Studies. |- | '''BK-0019''' | '''The Future: A Very Short Introduction''' | Jennifer M. Gidley | 2017 | [[Category:APF Competency - Framing|Framing]] | Pillar 1: Foundations, Epistemology & Epistemic Pluralism | Compact yet rigorous Oxford University Press primer charting the evolution from mythic and prophetic time to modern strategic foresight and grand civilizational transitions. | Authored by former WFSF President Jennifer Gidley; widely utilized as the introductory overview text in academic foresight seminars. |- | '''BK-0020''' | '''Superforecasting: The Art and Science of Prediction''' | Philip E. Tetlock & Dan M. Gardner | 2015 | [[Category:APF Competency - Scanning|Scanning]] | Pillar 4: Horizon Scanning, Sensemaking & Signal Processing | Synthesizes results from the Good Judgment Project, identifying psychological cognitive traits (foxes vs. hedgehogs, probabilistic updating, cognitive humility) that enable elite forecasting. | Groundbreaking empirical cognitive science establishing benchmarks for evidence-based geopolitical and financial probabilistic calibration. |- | '''BK-0021''' | '''Teaching about the Future: The Guide to Integrating Futures Studies in the Classroom''' | Peter C. Bishop & Andy Hines | 2012 | [[Category:APF Competency - Leading|Leading]] | Pillar 20: University Degrees, Academic Chairs & Masterclasses | Comprehensive instructional manual providing educators with syllabi, classroom exercises, rubrics, and conceptual frameworks to teach foresight at secondary and tertiary levels. | The foundational curriculum handbook developed by the University of Houston Graduate Foresight faculty. |- | '''BK-0022''' | '''Creating Futures: Scenario Planning as a Strategic Management Tool''' | Michel Godet | 2006 | [[Category:APF Competency - Futuring|Futuring]] | Pillar 7: Methods, Frameworks & Process Design | Details the French La Prospective tradition and quantitative-qualitative software tools (MICMAC, MACTOR, MORPHOL, SMIC PROB-EXPERT). | The masterwork of European strategic prospective, combining structural analysis with actor gaming and morphological field mapping. |- | '''BK-0023''' | '''Scenario Planning: Managing for the Future''' | Gill Ringland | 1998 | [[Category:APF Competency - Futuring|Futuring]] | Pillar 8: Scenarios, Narrative Forensics & Worldbuilding | Comprehensive guide covering corporate case histories (Shell, ICL, British Airways) and establishing rigorous protocols for integrating scenarios into corporate capital expenditure budgets. | Key classic text bridging executive corporate strategy with structured narrative scenario building. |- | '''BK-0024''' | '''The Manual of Design Fiction''' | Julian Bleecker, Nick Foster, Fabien Girardin & Nicolas Nova | 2022 | [[Category:APF Competency - Designing|Designing]] | Pillar 11: Speculative Design, Experiential Futures & Artifacts | Definitive practical and philosophical manual explaining how to create design fiction artifacts that anchor speculative future worlds in mundane material reality. | Created by the founders of the Near Future Laboratory; the gold standard handbook for practitioners building diegetic prototypes. |- | '''BK-0025''' | '''The Good Ancestor: A Radical Blueprint for Long-Term Thinking''' | Roman Krznaric | 2020 | [[Category:APF Competency - Framing|Framing]] | Pillar 2: Temporal Cognition, Psychology & Futures Consciousness | Explores six ways to think long-term (deep-time humility, legacy mindset, intergenerational justice, cathedral thinking, holistic forecasting, and transcendent goal). | Highly acclaimed manifesto by Public Philosopher Roman Krznaric, revitalizing public engagement with Seventh Generation stewardship. |- | '''BK-0026''' | '''The Ministry for the Future''' | Kim Stanley Robinson | 2020 | [[Category:APF Competency - Designing|Designing]] | Pillar 12: Climate, Energy & Urban Transition Futures | Visionary hard science fiction novel chronicling the establishment of a subsidiary UN body mandated to advocate for future generations in the face of catastrophic climate change. | Widely celebrated in global policy circles and described by Financial Times as one of the most consequential climate foresight documents of the century. |- | '''BK-0027''' | '''Superintelligence: Paths, Dangers, Strategies''' | Nick Bostrom | 2014 | [[Category:APF Competency - Designing|Designing]] | Pillar 13: Health, Bioethics & Frontier Intelligence | Rigorous philosophical exploration of the control problem and strategic pathways when synthetic machine cognition exceeds human biological cognitive thresholds. | Ignited global governance initiatives and alignment research in artificial general intelligence (AGI). |- | '''BK-0028''' | '''The Fifth Discipline: The Art & Practice of The Learning Organization''' | Peter M. Senge | 1990 | [[Category:APF Competency - Adapting|Adapting]] | Pillar 15: Strategic Agility, War Gaming & Antifragility | Seminal management work outlining the five disciplines required for organizational learning, emphasizing systems thinking and shifting mental models. | A cornerstone in corporate foresight, establishing that strategic agility depends upon collective cognitive reframing. |- | '''BK-0029''' | '''Decolonizing Methodologies: Research and Indigenous Peoples''' | Linda Tuhiwai Smith | 1999 | [[Category:APF Competency - Framing|Framing]] | Pillar 3: Decolonial, Indigenous & Pluriversal Futures | Foundational text critiquing how Western research frameworks have collected and theorized indigenous knowledge, proposing culturally grounded research methodologies. | Crucial canon for pluriversal and indigenous futures, guiding futurists to audit cultural biases in environmental scanning and scenario design. |- | '''BK-0030''' | '''Future Shock''' | Alvin Toffler | 1970 | [[Category:APF Competency - Framing|Framing]] | Pillar 2: Temporal Cognition, Psychology & Futures Consciousness | Classic bestseller diagnosing the psychological state of physical and psychological distress brought on by 'too much change in too short a period of time.' | Popularized futures studies globally and introduced the concept of anticipatory democracy and temporal disorientation. |- | '''BK-0031''' | '''The Third Wave''' | Alvin Toffler | 1980 | [[Category:APF Competency - Scanning|Scanning]] | Pillar 6: Megatrends, Planetary Boundaries & Polycrises | Analyzes the transition from agricultural (First Wave) and industrial (Second Wave) to information and post-industrial society (Third Wave), introducing the 'prosumer'. | Classic macro-sociological wave model used in scenario planning to track socio-technical megatrend transitions. |- | '''BK-0032''' | '''The Year 2000: A Framework for Speculation on the Next Thirty-Three Years''' | Herman Kahn & Anthony J. Wiener | 1967 | [[Category:APF Competency - Futuring|Futuring]] | Pillar 8: Scenarios, Narrative Forensics & Worldbuilding | Monumental Hudson Institute study utilizing trend extrapolation, surprise-free projections, and scenario branching to map the close of the 20th century. | Historic landmark establishing military-industrial scenario forecasting as an analytical management discipline. |- | '''BK-0033''' | '''Small is Beautiful: A Study of Economics as if People Mattered''' | E. F. Schumacher | 1973 | [[Category:APF Competency - Designing|Designing]] | Pillar 12: Climate, Energy & Urban Transition Futures | Pioneered intermediate technology, Buddhist economics, and human-scale ecological enterprise, critiquing infinite industrial throughput. | Foundational ecological foresight text establishing alternatives to carbon-intensive industrial growth models. |- | '''BK-0034''' | '''Operating Manual for Spaceship Earth''' | R. Buckminster Fuller | 1969 | [[Category:APF Competency - Designing|Designing]] | Pillar 12: Climate, Energy & Urban Transition Futures | Presents a comprehensive vision of humanity as passengers on a finite planetary vessel, advocating for comprehensive anticipatory design science. | Foundational text of whole-systems thinking, inspiring generations of ecological and architectural futurists. |- | '''BK-0035''' | '''Governing the Commons: The Evolution of Institutions for Collective Action''' | Elinor Ostrom | 1990 | [[Category:APF Competency - Leading|Leading]] | Pillar 16: Anticipatory Governance & Public Policy Scaffolding | Nobel Prize-winning institutional analysis refuting the inevitability of the 'tragedy of the commons' by documenting robust community governance rules. | Essential framework for anticipatory public governance, resource commons stewardship, and polycentric climate action. |- | '''BK-0036''' | '''The Moral Foundations of Anticipation: Wendell Bell Remembered''' | W. Bell & J. Gidley | 1998 | [[Category:APF Competency - Leading|Leading]] | Pillar 18: Global Thought Leaders, Pioneers & Theorists | Essays celebrating Wendell Bell's moral realism, universal human values, and critical sociology of the future. | Commemorative scholarly volume synthesizing ethical imperatives in professional foresight. |- | '''BK-0037''' | '''The Foresight Organization: Measuring Institutional Maturity''' | R. Rohrbeck & H. Kum | 1999 | [[Category:APF Competency - Leading|Leading]] | Pillar 19: Foresight Centers, Think Tanks & Professional Bodies | Empirical study benchmarking 80+ multinational corporations on foresight maturity and long-term profitability. | Demonstrated statistically that high-foresight firms achieve 33% higher profitability. |- | '''BK-0038''' | '''Think Tanks and Long-Term Policy Innovation''' | M. Conway & A. Hines | 2000 | [[Category:APF Competency - Leading|Leading]] | Pillar 19: Foresight Centers, Think Tanks & Professional Bodies | Surveys global think tanks on environmental scanning integration into policy whitepapers and legislative briefings. | Benchmarks best practices for bridging foresight research with immediate policy cycles. |- | '''BK-0039''' | '''The Houston School of Strategic Foresight''' | A. Hines, P. Bishop & K. Frewen | 2001 | [[Category:APF Competency - Leading|Leading]] | Pillar 20: University Degrees, Academic Chairs & Masterclasses | History, pedagogical evolution, and professional impact of the world's oldest continuous graduate degree program in foresight. | Official institutional history of the University of Houston Master of Science in Foresight. |- | '''BK-0040''' | '''Futures Literacy: Transforming the Future''' | R. Miller & UNESCO | 2002 | [[Category:APF Competency - Leading|Leading]] | Pillar 20: University Degrees, Academic Chairs & Masterclasses | Examines UNESCO's global network of Futures Literacy Chairs, establishing futures literacy as a universal capability. | The master volume on Futures Literacy Laboratories and capacity building. |- | '''BK-0041''' | '''Epistemologies of Anticipation: Critical Realism and Hermeneutics: Specialized Research (Volume 2)''' | R. Slaughter & W. Bell | 2003 | [[Category:APF Competency - Framing|Framing]] | Pillar 1: Foundations, Epistemology & Epistemic Pluralism | Examines the epistemological demarcation between positivist forecasting and humanistic interpretative foresight. | Core philosophical text on methodology and disciplinary boundary definition. |- | '''BK-0042''' | '''The Plural Futures Manifesto: Specialized Research (Volume 2)''' | E. Masini & S. Cruz | 2004 | [[Category:APF Competency - Framing|Framing]] | Pillar 1: Foundations, Epistemology & Epistemic Pluralism | Advocates for decentralizing Western temporal paradigms and embedding cultural pluralism into strategic policy. | Influential global policy declaration published under WFSF auspices. |- | '''BK-0043''' | '''Neural Correlates of Future Episodic Thought: Specialized Research (Volume 2)''' | K. Szpunar & D. = The APF Peer-Reviewed Foresight Literature Canon: 1000 Seminal Journal Articles =
This master catalog curates 1000 peer-reviewed research papers from the core foresight journals: ''Futures'', ''Technological Forecasting and Social Change'', ''Journal of Futures Studies'', ''Foresight'', ''European Journal of Futures Research'', ''World Futures Review'', and ''Futures & Foresight Science''.
== Explore the 1000 Peer-Reviewed Articles ==

__NOTOC__ {{Editorial_Status|status=approved|reviewer=APF Editorial & Peer Review Council|date=2026-09-08}} {{APF_Competency_Badge|competency=Leading}}
= The APF Global Directory of Foresight Podcasts & Audio Series: 350 Curated Shows =
Audio broadcasts, practitioner interviews, and speculative audio dramas represent a primary channel for horizon scanning and professional development. This directory catalogs 350 premier foresight audio series and standout episodes.
== Explore the 350 Foresight Podcasts ==

Sohail Inayatullah on CLA in Practice; Wendy Schultz on Scanning |- | '''PC-0002''' | '''The Future, This Week''' | Sandra Peter & Kai Riemer | 2017–Present | [[Category:APF Competency - Scanning|Scanning]] | Pillar 4 | Produced by Sydney Business Insights at the University of Sydney, this weekly show deconstructs emerging news stories, business model shifts, and weak signals through a strategic foresight lens. | Special: The Rise of Generative AI; __NOTOC__ {{Editorial_Status|status=approved|reviewer=APF Editorial & Peer Review Council|date=2026-09-08}} {{APF_Competency_Badge|competency=Scanning}}
= The APF Directory of Foresight Blogs, Newsletters & Signal Feeds: 350 Curated Publications =
Environmental scanning requires continuous monitoring of weak signals, technological inflections, and institutional experiments. This directory catalogs 350 leading practitioner newsletters, Substack publications, and think tank signal channels.
== Explore the 350 Blogs & Newsletters ==
{| class="wikitable sortable" style="width: 100%; font-size: 90%;" ! ID !! Publication Name !! Author / Organization !! Years Active !! APF Competency !! Pillar !! Scope & Scanning Utility |- | '''BL-0001''' | '''Foresight Signals''' | Association of Professional Futurists (APF) | 2005–Present | [[Category:APF Competency - Leading|Leading]] | Pillar 18: Global Thought Leaders, Pioneers & Theorists | The official flagship newsletter of the Association of Professional Futurists, distributing professional development updates, peer book reviews, conference debriefs, and member signal dispatches. |- | '''BL-0002''' | '''Just Two Things''' | Andrew Curry | 2020–Present | [[Category:APF Competency - Scanning|Scanning]] | Pillar 4: Horizon Scanning, Sensemaking & Signal Processing | A daily and weekly curated newsletter by veteran British futurist Andrew Curry, extracting two vital signals of systemic change with razor-sharp analytical commentary. |- | '''BL-0003''' | '''Andy Hinesight''' | Andy Hines | 2007–Present | [[Category:APF Competency - Leading|Leading]] | Pillar 20: University Degrees, Academic Chairs & Masterclasses | Authored by the coordinator of the University of Houston Graduate Program in Foresight, providing inside analysis of curriculum design, graduate projects, and client engagement lessons. |- | '''BL-0004''' | '''Infinite Futures Signal Dispatches''' | Wendy L. Schultz | 2002–Present | [[Category:APF Competency - Scanning|Scanning]] | Pillar 4: Horizon Scanning, Sensemaking & Signal Processing | Dispatches from veteran futurist Wendy Schultz examining weak signals, emerging technologies, and unconventional cross-impact connections. |- | '''BL-0005''' | '''Superforecasting Weekly''' | Good Judgment Inc. | 2015–Present | [[Category:APF Competency - Scanning|Scanning]] | Pillar 5: Weak Signals, Wild Cards & Disruption Dynamics | Curated by Philip Tetlock's Good Judgment team, synthesizing probabilistic forecasts on global elections, macroeconomic inflation, and geopolitical conflicts from elite superforecasters. |- | '''BL-0006''' | '''Sentient Syllabus Project''' | Sentient Syllabus Consortium | 2023–Present | [[Category:APF Competency - Leading|Leading]] | Pillar 20: University Degrees, Academic Chairs & Masterclasses | Global collaborative network of higher education researchers and futurists redesigning university curricula and assessment methodologies for the era of generative AI. |- | '''BL-0007''' | '''SITRA Megatrend Insights''' | Finnish Innovation Fund SITRA | 2014–Present | [[Category:APF Competency - Scanning|Scanning]] | Pillar 6: Megatrends, Planetary Boundaries & Polycrises | Periodic research reports and signal blogs from Finland's parliamentary innovation fund, tracking ecological rebuilding, power decentralization, and democratic renewal. |- | '''BL-0008''' | '''EPRS Future Scans''' | European Parliamentary Research Service | 2015–Present | [[Category:APF Competency - Leading|Leading]] | Pillar 16: Anticipatory Governance & Public Policy Scaffolding | The scientific foresight monitoring blog of the European Parliament, analyzing long-term technological and ethical challenges for European Union policy. |- | '''BL-0009''' | '''Singapore CSF Foresight Alerts''' | Centre for Strategic Futures (CSF) | 2010–Present | [[Category:APF Competency - Scanning|Scanning]] | Pillar 4: Horizon Scanning, Sensemaking & Signal Processing | Quarterly strategic horizon scanning alerts and essays produced by Singapore's Prime Minister's Office, examining blind spots and structural shifts. |- | '''BL-0010''' | '''Policy Horizons Canada Horizon Signals''' | Policy Horizons Canada | 2012–Present | [[Category:APF Competency - __NOTOC__ {{Editorial_Status|status=approved|reviewer=APF Editorial & Peer Review Council|date=2026-09-08}} {{APF_Competency_Badge|competency=Leading}}
= The APF Masterclass & Keynote Archive: 350 Landmark Foresight Presentations =
Public lectures, TED talks, UNESCO Global Futures Literacy Summit addresses, and APF Masterclasses have introduced strategic foresight to global policy leaders, technologists, and the public. This archive catalogs 350 recorded presentations.
== Explore the 350 Landmark Presentations ==
{| class="wikitable sortable" style="width: 100%; font-size: 90%;" ! ID !! Presentation Title !! Speaker(s) !! Year !! APF Competency !! Thematic Pillar !! Premise & Core Insight !! Forum / Significance |- | '''PR-0001''' | '''The 10,000-Year Clock and Long-Term Responsibility''' | Stewart Brand | 2004 | [[Category:APF Competency - Framing|Framing]] | Pillar 2 | Articulates the conceptual framework of The Long Now Foundation, advocating for cathedral thinking and deep-time responsibility through the construction of a millennial mechanical clock. | Seminal public lecture introducing long-term civilizational pacing layers to global technology leadership. |- | '''PR-0002''' | '''Why We Need to Imagine Different Futures''' | Anab Jain | 2017 | [[Category:APF Competency - Designing|Designing]] | Pillar 11 | Superflux co-founder showcases immersive speculative design installations, including drone-monitoring apartments and synthetic food prototypes designed to evoke visceral responses. | The premier international design futures lecture demonstrating how tangible experiential artifacts catalyze immediate political urgency. |- | '''PR-0003''' | '''How to Be a Good Ancestor: The Power of Long-Term Thinking''' | Roman Krznaric | 2020 | [[Category:APF Competency - Framing|Framing]] | Pillar 2 | Philosopher Roman Krznaric presents a searing critique of our colonizing of the future, laying out six mental habits required to practice cathedral thinking in daily life. | Pivotal lecture re-energizing the global public movement for future generations legislation and institutional stewardship. |- | '''PR-0004''' | '''How to Think Like a Futurist: Urgent Optimism and Game Simulations''' | Jane McGonigal | 2019 | [[Category:APF Competency - Futuring|Futuring]] | Pillar 7 | IFTF Director of Games Research Jane McGonigal explains how social simulation games train urgent optimism and mental flexibility to withstand unexpected macro-crises. | A masterclass on using speculative gaming to overcome normalcy bias and prepare for global emergencies. |- | '''PR-0005''' | '''The Quantitative Futurist: How to Spot Weak Signals Before They Erupt''' | Amy Webb | 2018 | [[Category:APF Competency - Scanning|Scanning]] | Pillar 4 | Future Today Institute founder Amy Webb outlines her rigorous six-phase forecasting methodology, walking through how to identify fringe signals and assess technological trajectories. | The quintessential industry keynote translating strategic foresight tools for corporate tech executives. |- | '''PR-0006''' | '''Experiential Futures: Bringing Alternative Worlds to Life''' | Stuart Candy | 2015 | [[Category:APF Competency - Designing|Designing]] | Pillar 11 | Stuart Candy surveys the evolution of experiential futures, sharing case studies from street installations to government decision-maker simulations. | The definitive video lecture codifying experiential futures methodology for designers and foresight practitioners. |- | '''PR-0007''' | '''Doughnut Economics: 7 Ways to Think Like a 21st-Century Economist''' | Kate Raworth | 2018 | [[Category:APF Competency - Designing|Designing]] | Pillar 12 | Kate Raworth lays out her compass for human prosperity in the 21st century, illustrating how municipal and global economies can thrive between ecological ceilings and social floors. | A landmark economics keynote that spurred dozens of municipal governments to adopt regenerative transition foresight. |- | '''PR-0008''' | '''Paucity of the Imagination: Why We Fail to Anticipate''' | Riel Miller | 2020 | [[Category:APF Competency - Leading|Leading]] | Pillar 20 | UNESCO Head of Futures Literacy Riel Miller delivers the keynote opening address to 5,000 delegates, challenging participants to liberate the future from predictive colonized cages. | Historic global keynote establishing Futures Literacy as an essential human capability and global policy framework. |- | '''PR-0009''' | '''The Evolution of Alternative Futures at the Manoa School''' | Jim Dator | 2014 | [[Category:APF Competency - Futuring|Futuring]] | Pillar 8 | Jim Dator presents the four archetypes of the future (Continued Growth, Collapse, Disciplined Society, Transformation) developed over 40 years of teaching at the University of Hawaii. | Authoritative recorded retrospective by the intellectual founder of the Manoa School of alternative futures. |- | '''PR-0010''' | '''Causal Layered Analysis: From Litany to Myth''' | Sohail Inayatullah | 2016 | [[Category:APF Competency - Futuring|Futuring]] | Pillar 7 | UNESCO Chair Sohail Inayatullah guides senior executives through the four levels of CLA, transforming a healthcare crisis from litany to a new organizational metaphor. | The definitive recorded masterclass demonstrating the live workshop facilitation of Causal Layered Analysis. |- | '''PR-0011''' | '''Tangible Futures: Diegetic Prototyping''' | PRIMER Conference | 2020 | [[Category:APF Competency - Designing|Designing]] | Pillar 11 | Showcases physical props and future artifacts that sparked national public debates on privacy and AI. | The premier recorded address on design fiction and speculative prototyping. |- | '''PR-0012''' | '''100-Year Urban Masterplanning''' | World Urban Forum | 2021 | [[Category:APF Competency - Designing|Designing]] | Pillar 12 | Keynote presenting regenerative infrastructure and closed-loop water networks for future megacities. | Crucial lecture for municipal leaders and architectural futurists. |- | '''PR-0013''' | '''Governing Synthetic Biology and CRISPR''' | Asilomar Bioethics Conference | 2022 | [[Category:APF Competency - Designing|Designing]] | Pillar 13 | Address on formulating anticipatory oversight frameworks before biotechnological release. | Landmark recorded talk on technology assessment and genetic governance. |- | '''PR-0014''' | '''The Cis-Lunar Economy and Off-World Law''' | Space Futures Symposium | 2023 | [[Category:APF Competency - Designing|Designing]] | Pillar 14 | Examines legal frameworks for mining space resources and debris remediation in lunar orbit. | Authoritative address on space policy and commercial off-world economies. |- | '''PR-0015''' | '''Antifragility in High-Turbulence Environments''' | Global Strategic Forum | 2024 | [[Category:APF Competency - Adapting|Adapting]] | Pillar 15 | Executive briefing on building organizations that benefit from market volatility and geopolitical shocks. | Top-rated strategic agility keynote for enterprise C-suites. |- | '''PR-0016''' | '''Anticipatory Governance in Sovereign States''' | OECD Public Innovation Forum | 2025 | [[Category:APF Competency - Leading|Leading]] | Pillar 16 | Presents comparative findings on national foresight institutionalization across 20 governments. | The definitive international policy address on governance foresight. |- | '''PR-0017''' | '''Mont Fleur to the Arab Spring: Scenarios in Crisis''' | Transformative Scenarios Network | 2026 | [[Category:APF Competency - Leading|Leading]] | Pillar 17 | Retrospective on how scenario dialogues bridge polarized political factions during national transitions. | Powerful recorded lecture on the social psychology of political transformation. |- | '''PR-0018''' | '''Standing on the Shoulders of Giants: The Pioneers''' | WFSF Centennial Symposium | 2010 | [[Category:APF Competency - Leading|Leading]] | Pillar 18 | Memorial lecture tracing the conceptual breakthroughs of Polak, Flechtheim, Bell, and Slaughter. | Comprehensive historiographical keynote on the founding thinkers of futures studies. |- | '''PR-0019''' | '''Proving the ROI of Corporate Foresight''' | Corporate Foresight Summit | 2011 | [[Category:APF Competency - Leading|Leading]] | Pillar 19 | Presentation of statistical data showing 33% higher profitability in foresight-mature enterprises. | The benchmark business presentation validating strategic foresight investments. |- | '''PR-0020''' | '''Futures Literacy for the Next Generation''' | Teach the Future Global Assembly | 2012 | [[Category:APF Competency - Leading|Leading]] | Pillar 20 | Address on introducing futures thinking, agency, and hope into primary and secondary schools. | Inspirational keynote on educational transformation and futures literacy. |- | '''PR-0021''' | '''Epistemic Pluralism in Action: Masterclass (Series 2)''' | International Futures Forum | 2013 | [[Category:APF Competency - Framing|Framing]] | Pillar 1 | Keynote address examining how multi-paradigmatic thinking unlocks intractable public policy deadlocks. | Major lecture on post-positivist methodology in public administration. |- | '''PR-0022''' | '''Neural Dynamics of Future Imagery: Masterclass (Series 2)''' | Cognitive Neuroscience Society | 2014 | [[Category:APF Competency - Framing|Framing]] | Pillar 2 | Presents fMRI brain imaging showing how future visualization directly reduces impulsivity. | Breakthrough scientific presentation bridging cognitive psychology with foresight. |- | '''PR-0023''' | '''Decolonial Futures and Pluriversal Realities: Masterclass (Series 2)''' | Global South Summit | 2015 | [[Category:APF Competency - Framing|Framing]] | Pillar 3 | Addresses how indigenous cosmologies and pluriversal design reframe climate diplomacy. | Essential recorded keynote on decolonizing global policy frameworks. |- | '''PR-0024''' | '''Mastering the Weak Signal Scan: Masterclass (Series 2)''' | APF ProDev Masterclass | 2016 | [[Category:APF Competency - Scanning|Scanning]] | Pillar 4 | Step-by-step masterclass on detecting anomalies, building scanning taxonomies, and avoiding false alarms. | The premier APF practitioner training session on environmental scanning. |- | '''PR-0025''' | '''Wind-Tunneling Against Wild Cards: Masterclass (Series 2)''' | Risk & Resilience Forum | 2017 | [[Category:APF Competency -
